The Bears are regrouping after a decisive 34-13 road loss to Western Kentucky, while the Owls hope to rebound from a heartbreaking 27-26 defeat at the hands of Jacksonville State. Rickie Collins is the engine for Kennesaw State. Most recently, they lost 27-26 to Jacksonville State in their league opener. The Missouri State Bears (1-4, 0-1 CUSA), meanwhile, were a surprising bowl team last year in their first season at the FBS level. However, with a new coaching staff this season, they've struggled and are still looking for their first FBS win. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 4 Ohio State is looking for revenge against No. 5 Indiana after last year's Big Ten title game Getty Images The 100th all-time meeting between Ohio State and Indiana should be a good one. The No. 5 Hoosiers host the fourth-ranked Buckeys with their undefeated record on the line. The winner will have the inside track to Indianapolis. The reigning national champion, Indiana, hasn't faced a single ranked team, and it's had one of the easier schedules in the Big Ten. The Hoosiers did get a dicey road test against Nebraska last weekend, but that was a nice warm-up for what's to come on Saturday. Despite losing a number of key pieces from last year's team, Indiana still looks like a serious title contender thanks to newcomers Nick Marsh (528 receiving yards and six touchdowns), Turbo Richard (leads Big Ten in rushing yards) and Tobi Osunsanmi (leads the Big Ten in sacks and tackles for loss). Ohio State will be looking for a little revenge after losing to Indiana in the 2025 Big Ten Championship. That loss snapped the Buckeyes' 30-game winning streak over the Hoosiers, so they'll try to start a new one on Saturday. That's entirely possible, largely due to the presence of Heisman Trophy favorite and athletic anomaly Jeremiah Smith , who leads the conference in just about every major receiving category. This is one of the best games on a loaded Week 7 slate, so here is everything you must know as No. 5 Indiana visits No. 4 Ohio State. Ohio State vs. Indiana: Need to know Annual top-five matchup: For the first 97 meetings between these teams, there were zero top-five matchups. When the game kicks off Saturday, it will be the third time in as many years that Indiana and Ohio State have played with both teams ranked inside the top five. If we're honest, Indiana was the main reason there were no top-five matchups in the first 97 meetings, but that has changed in a big way now. The Hoosiers have the resources and the coach to compete with the Buckeyes, so we may have a budding Big Ten rivalry on our hands. Smith's historic season: Every week, Smith rewrites the record books at the program, conference and NCAA level. That could continue on Saturday because Smith is just one receiving touchdown shy of matching Michigan legend Braylon Edwards for the most in Big Ten history (39). Smith has already secured the school records for career receptions (211), receiving yards (3,474) and receiving touchdowns (38). He should only add to those totals against a Hoosiers secondary Smith beat for 144 yards last year. Sacking Sayin: One way to make sure Smith never gets the football is to hit Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin while he still has the ball. That's exactly what the Hoosiers did in the Big Ten title game, sacking Sayin five times. Indiana has the personnel to get after Sayin again this time around. Osunsanmi and Stephen Daley have combined for 10 sacks, and Ohio State has allowed 11 sacks of Sayin thus far. The battle between the Indiana defensive front and the Ohio State offensive line in pass protection will be critical. Having said that, I do wonder how well Indiana's passing defense will hold up for 60 minutes, especially without D'Angelo Ponds in the secondary this time. Ohio State hits enough big plays with Smith to create some breathing room late. Can the Hoosiers take down the Buckeyes ? If so, they’ll need most of these predictions to come to fruition. 3 bold predictions for Indiana vs. Ohio State Maryland Terrapins linebacker Daniel Wingate (1) hits Ohio State Buckeyes quarterback Julian Sayin (10) during the NCAA football game at Ohio Stadium in Columbus on Oct. 10, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Indiana sacks Julian Sayin five times Indiana sacks Julian Sayin five times In the 2025 regular season, Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin was sacked six total times in 12 games. Indiana’s defense got to him five times in the Big Ten Championship Game alone. This 2026 matchup should be more of the same – if not an even more dominant showing from the Hoosiers’ pass-rushing attack. Halfway through the regular season, Sayin has already been sacked 11 times. And Indiana has a whopping 20 sacks in six games. The writing is on the wall – in Sharpie. Expect the Hoosiers to apply a lot of pressure on Sayin. It’ll be interesting to see how Sayin responds, especially considering he’s shown off his legs more often this year (and Indiana has been vulnerable to QBs who take off). Neither team scores more than 17 points Oct 10, 2026; Lincoln, Nebraska, USA; Indiana Hoosiers head coach Curt Cignetti looks on during a timeout against the Nebraska Cornhuskers during the second quarter at Memorial Stadium. In the 2025 conference title game, these two teams combined for 23 points in an old-fashioned, rugged Big Ten slugfest. But this Ohio State offense is operating at a different level. It has put up at least 31 points in every league game thus far. Sayin and stud wide receiver Jeremiah Smith have been flat-out unstoppable. As for the Hoosiers, they have scored at least 20 in every outing in 2026. Then again, Indiana scored six points through three quarters last Saturday at Nebraska. And, on the flip side, Ohio State hasn’t seen a defense half as sturdy as Indiana’s, aside from Texas, which held the Buckeyes to only three points in the second half. If Indiana’s defense strings together four full quarters, it can bottle up this Ohio State offense – or at least keep it at bay (Smith won’t be entirely shut down by any defense this year). And the expectation is that the Hoosiers offense, which has sputtered at times this year, struggles with this Buckeyes defense. It’d be a surprise to see either team score three touchdowns. The Hoosiers keep Ohio State under 100 yards on the ground Oct 3, 2026; Piscataway, New Jersey, USA; Indiana Hoosiers defensive lineman Stephen Daley (9) celebrates a sick with defensive end Tobi Osunsanmi (12) during the second half against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights at SHI Stadium. Indiana, which is holding opponents to a Big Ten best 75.0 rushing yards per game, has been an absolute brick wall against the run. Ohio State, meanwhile, hasn’t exactly been running through anybody. It managed just 94 rushing yards against Texas in Week 2. Kent State held the Buckeyes to 3.8 yards per carry. You get the idea. In general, Ohio State’s experienced offensive line has been surprisingly uninspiring in 2026. Expect Indiana’s elite defensive front to have its way getting after Sayin and stifling the run game. But can the Hoosiers do enough against Smith? That will be the question. picks.blurb: Rece Davis Reveals Ohio State-Indiana Pick for 'Biggest Game' in Bloomington History Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS ESPN College GameDay host Rece Davis picked Ohio State to win at Indiana on Saturday, siding with the Buckeyes in a top-five showdown that puts the Hoosiers’ 22-game winning streak on the line in Bloomington. On the College GameDay podcast, Davis joined fellow panelists Pete Thamel and Dan Wetzel in taking No. 4 Ohio State (5-1) over No. 5 Indiana (6-0), though he expects a close finish. “I think a field goal at the end decides it one way or the other,” Davis said. Rece Davis explains his Ohio State pick Ohio State head coach Ryan Day takes the team out of the tunnel before the game against the Maryland Terrapins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Davis called Saturday’s noon ET kickoff on Fox the “ biggest game in the history of Bloomington , Indiana, not played on a basketball court.” It’s a rematch of last December’s Big Ten championship game, which Indiana won 13-10 in Indianapolis on its way to the national title. Davis called Saturday’s noon ET kickoff on Fox the “ biggest game in the history of Bloomington , Indiana, not played on a basketball court.” It’s a rematch of last December’s Big Ten championship game, which Indiana won 13-10 in Indianapolis on its way to the national title. His case against the Hoosiers rests on the streak itself. “When you have a winning streak as long as Indiana’s, longest in the country ... you start having these near misses,” Davis said. “Sooner or later, one gets you, and it can almost reset you a little bit.” Indiana held off Northwestern 29-23 in its Big Ten opener after starting running back Turbo Richard left with an injury, leaning on backup Lee Beebe Jr. for 203 rushing yards. Last Saturday in Lincoln, Indiana trailed Nebraska 17-6 in the fourth quarter before quarterback Josh Hoover hit receiver Nick Marsh for touchdowns of 75 and 44 yards, the second on fourth-and-1. Afterward, Indiana coach Curt Cignetti said his players “ took a deep breath and relaxed and forgot all the garbage in the first half.” Can Ohio State protect Julian Sayin? Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin (10) throws during the college football game against the Maryland Terrapins | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Davis pointed to the Buckeyes’ offensive line as the deciding matchup. “Ohio State has allowed pressure on 27% of its dropbacks this season. That’s 14th in the Big Ten,” Davis said. “That’s not a great formula against Indiana. Indiana does an unbelievable job of getting pressure without blitzing.” Davis pointed to the Buckeyes’ offensive line as the deciding matchup. “Ohio State has allowed pressure on 27% of its dropbacks this season. That’s 14th in the Big Ten,” Davis said. “That’s not a great formula against Indiana. Indiana does an unbelievable job of getting pressure without blitzing.” Indiana leads the Big Ten with 20 sacks, while Ohio State has allowed 11, which ranks 14th in the conference . The Hoosiers also finished last December’s 13-10 win with five sacks and nine tackles for loss. Still, the Buckeyes have done damage when the pocket holds. Quarterback Julian Sayin, who holds No. 1 in our Big Ten quarterback rankings , has thrown for 1,772 yards and 17 touchdowns, and wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has 916 receiving yards and 11 touchdown catches. Ohio State’s offense also ranks second nationally in expected points added per pass, while Indiana’s defense ranks 76th in that measure. And the Buckeyes’ line landed on the Joe Moore Award midseason honor roll on Wednesday. Why Davis still backs Indiana’s offense Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover (10) passes against the Nebraska Cornhuskers | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Davis pushed back on the idea that Indiana’s attack has slipped, comparing Hoover to Fernando Mendoza, who quarterbacked the Hoosiers to last season’s title. Davis pushed back on the idea that Indiana’s attack has slipped, comparing Hoover to Fernando Mendoza, who quarterbacked the Hoosiers to last season’s title. “If Josh Hoover plays 16 games, as Fernando did last year, the numbers are going to be pretty much the same, almost the same,” Davis said. “He’s thrown 17 touchdown passes. I think Fernando finished with 41 last year. You double that to the end of the season, you’re at 34, and then you have the playoff.” Davis also noted that Indiana remains a run-first team. “Turbo Richard leads the conference in runs of 20 yards or longer,” he said. “They average over six yards a carry.” He placed the matchup in rare Big Ten company, too. “Only once have two teams played three consecutive seasons and been in the top five of the AP poll in all three meetings: Michigan and Ohio State in the middle of the legendary Ten-Year War between Bo Schembechler and Woody Hayes,” Davis said. ESPN analyst Greg McElroy took the opposite side this week, picking Indiana as the underdog to extend its streak to 23 games. My Ohio State vs. Indiana prediction is riding with the home underdog as Bloomington takes center stage for a historic showdown. Saturday's noon ET clash on FOX's Big Noon Saturday marks Memorial Stadium's first-ever top-five matchup, and the Hoosiers are looking to make it one to remember. The Buckeyes arrive in Bloomington as 3.5-point favorites, but the Hoosiers have matchup advantages and Curt Cignetti's track record on their side. TOP PICK Who will win Ohio State vs Indiana: Indiana +3.5 I'm locking in a trade on the Indiana Hoosiers at +3.5 over the Ohio State Buckeyes and would play them down to a pick'em. Indiana has a strength-on-weakness edge over Ohio State in pass protection, and the Hoosiers have better standard-down success and line-yards-per-snap differentials , per GameOnPaper.com . Meanwhile, Indiana's defense can make the Buckeyes one-dimensional on offense. The Hoosiers rank sixth in the country in defensive rushing success rate, and Ohio State is only 81st in yards per rush. I also trust Curt Cignetti more in this spot. He's 6-2 straight up and 5-3 against the spread vs. top-10 opponents at Indiana , with a +13.8 spread differential. The Hoosiers beat Ohio State 13-10 in the 2025 Big Ten title game, and now get the Buckeyes at home with points. Ohio State vs Indiana Over/Under pick: Over 49.5 I'd play the Over at any total below 51.5 . Thursday night’s availability report brought good news for the Buckeyes. West, freshman defensive end Khary Wilder, and backup offensive lineman Deontae Armstrong were all listed as questionable Wednesday. All three have since been removed from the report and are expected to play against Indiana. West’s status is the one that's getting the attention here. He’ll need to be ready to handle a real share of the carries against a strong Indiana defensive front. Keeping Bo Jackson fresh is going to be key in a game of this size. Having West available gives Ohio State a second back instead of pushing a deeper option into a bigger role on the road. Wide receiver Brock Boyd is the only other notable Buckeye still listed as questionable to play against Indiana. On the flip side, Ohio State will have five starters back who didn’t play a week ago against Maryland. Wide receivers Brandon Inniss and Devin McCuin, cornerback Jay Timmons, linebacker Christian Alliegro, and offensive lineman Phillip Daniels will all return against the Hoosiers. That’s a significant boost across the lineup. Inniss and McCuin give the passing game two more targets, and Timmons and Alliegro return to a defense that will face one of its toughest tests yet. Daniels coming back also helps an offensive line that will be without Siereveld. Midweek wasn't great at all for Ohio State on the injury front, but the latest news did bring welcomed news for the Buckeyes. Ohio State is heading into a top-5 matchup with the Hoosiers that will shape the Big Ten race at the end of the season. The Buckeyes need to be as healthy as possible for it. Isaiah West cleared to play against Indiana Ohio State gets 5 starters back from the Maryland game Siereveld and Ja'Kobi Jackson are still the two notable absences for Ohio State heading into Bloomington. Thursday night’s availability report brought good news for the Buckeyes. West, freshman defensive end Khary Wilder, and backup offensive lineman Deontae Armstrong were all listed as questionable Wednesday. All three have since been removed from the report and are expected to play against Indiana. West’s status is the one that's getting the attention here. He has 22 carries for 80 rushing yards and one touchdown. With Ja'Kobi Jackson out, West will be Ohio State’s second running back in this game. He’ll need to be ready to handle a real share of the carries against a strong Indiana defensive front. Keeping Bo Jackson fresh is going to be key in a game of this size. Having West available gives Ohio State a second back instead of pushing a deeper option into a bigger role on the road. Wide receiver Brock Boyd is the only other notable Buckeye still listed as questionable to play against Indiana. On the flip side, Ohio State will have five starters back who didn’t play a week ago against Maryland. Wide receivers Brandon Inniss and Devin McCuin, cornerback Jay Timmons, linebacker Christian Alliegro, and offensive lineman Phillip Daniels will all return against the Hoosiers. That’s a significant boost across the lineup. Inniss and McCuin give the passing game two more targets, and Timmons and Alliegro return to a defense that will face one of its toughest tests yet. Daniels coming back also helps an offensive line that will be without Siereveld. Midweek wasn't great at all for Ohio State on the injury front, but the latest news did bring welcomed news for the Buckeyes. Ohio State is heading into a top-5 matchup with the Hoosiers that will shape the Big Ten race at the end of the season. The Buckeyes need to be as healthy as possible for it. Isaiah West cleared to play against Indiana Ohio State gets 5 starters back from the Maryland game Siereveld and Ja'Kobi Jackson are still the two notable absences for Ohio State heading into Bloomington. Losing a starting offensive lineman and a running back at the same time puts more pressure on the run game against a defense that has been tough up front. Still, getting West off the availability report is welcome news for the Buckeyes. Ohio State is going to need its run game Saturday in Bloomington, and the backfield now has more depth than it appeared to have Wednesday. How the Buckeyes split the carries between Bo Jackson and West against Indiana’s front will be worth watching. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. picks.headline: Florida vs. Texas Final Score Predictions: Experts weigh in on a desperate Gators team heading to Austin
picks.blurb: Florida vs. Texas Final Score Predictions: Experts weigh in on a desperate Gators team heading to Austin - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Alan Youngblood/Gainesville Sun-Imagn Images, Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Brandon Little, Craig Smith, Justin Churchill, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness Thu, October 15, 2026 at 6:48 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After suffering back-to-back embarrassing losses, can the Florida Gators get back in the win column against a reeling Texas Longhorns team? The Florida Gators are in a rough spot at 4-2 as they head to Austin to take on the Texas Longhorns on Saturday afternoon. After two blowout losses to the Missouri Tigers and South Carolina Gamecocks on homecoming, Jon Sumrall 's team is in a tough spot. They were at one point being talked about as potentially being the 2019 LSU Tigers from on the precipice of collapsing. It's his first year at the helm, and the talent level still isn't quite there yet. For the Longhorns, they have beaten Ohio State, but are coming off a tough loss in the Red River Rivalry to the Oklahoma Sooners. They are in an interesting spot right now, and a win is a must for both teams. Who will get the win? Our experts made their predictions. Texas 38, Florida 24 Can we trust the Florida Gators? Honestly, no, and that includes the four-game winning streak to start the season with a massive blowout win over Ole Miss. The defense is struggling to generate pressure and the coverage on the back end has been incredibly inconsistent. Even with Texas having lost Red River last week, their success so far this season and offensive talent gets the Longhorns the win. Can the Gators get the win? Absolutely! Will they? I doubt it. – Tyler Forness , A to Z Florida Texas 33, Florida 19 Both teams come in off dismal losses to unranked teams. The Longhorns, who haven't looked dominant this year by any means, gagged away a game they should have won against Oklahoma but for a pick six and a punt block touchdown. Florida got mollywhopped by South Carolina one game after getting throttled by Missouri. As such, it's tough to tell up from down with these two teams. But my mind immediately goes to two things. First, the Horns' front is still nasty, and Florida suddenly can't find any space for Jadan Baugh and the ground game. On the other side, Florida's defense has become a sieve, and I don't trust they've found a way to fix it yet. Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo are too much for the Longhorns, who win comfortably in Austin. – Craig Smith , A to Z Miami Texas 31, Florida 20 Arch Manning has faced plenty of criticism for his inconsistency this season, but this is the type of matchup that could help him get back on track. Florida's pass defense has been a major weakness, and I expect Manning to take full advantage by delivering his best performance of the 2026 season. The Longhorns have the talent to exploit the Gators' struggling secondary, and Manning should find plenty of opportunities to push the ball downfield and put points on the board. After an uneven stretch offensively, this could be the breakthrough performance Texas needs. Florida should have some success early, particularly with running back Jadan Baugh leading the way. Baugh has been one of the Gators' most productive playmakers, and I expect him to help Florida move the ball and keep the game competitive in the first half. However, Texas has the defensive talent to make adjustments and limit Florida's offensive production as the game progresses. The Gators have struggled to maintain consistency in recent weeks, and that issue will catch up with them again in Austin. Texas pulls away in the second half, with Manning and the offense doing enough to secure a much-needed win. – Ryan Roberts , A to Z Notre Dame Texas 21, Florida 17 The Gators have fallen off a bit in the last few weeks after starting red hot. Texas is coming off a disappointing loss to Oklahoma. So, you know, Steve Sarkisian is going to be looking to get his team rolling again. Last week probably showed Texas what they should be doing more often on offense. They need to run more quick-game stuff with Arch Manning, because the long, developing routes downfield aren't helping the offense. Their offensive line isn't great, so they need to start running more quick-game plays. I think this past game showed some of that, and Texas still gets the win despite the offense struggling against a decent Florida defense. – Justin Churchill , A to Z Oklahoma Texas 30, Florida 20 As high as I was on the Florida Gators after the Ole Miss win, that hype has come crashing down after games against Missouri and South Carolina. The offense, led by Jadan Baugh, simply hasn't looked the same, and now the availability of starting QB Aaron Philo is in question. As for Texas, the Longhorns are coming off an embarrassing loss of their own after losing Red River to a bad OU team, and they aim to get back on track. Florida's defense has been bad, to say the least, and this game may serve as a great game for Arch Manning nd Texas. Give me the Longhorns here. – Rob Gregson , A to Z Alabama Texas 28, Florida 17 Texas and Florida both need wins this week, and the pressure is even higher for Steve Sarkisian and Arch Manning. Two losses for Texas at this point in the season would make things very uncomfortable in Austin, and perhaps it would mark the beginning of the end for some important names there. I don't think that's going to happen, though. I think Texas bounces back this week behind a strong defensive performance and looks the part against Florida. If the Longhorns can limit Jaden Baugh, they'll defend home field without much issue. I think Florida hangs around, but the Longhorns put it away in the fourth quarter. – Brandon Little , A to Z Ohio State Final Prediction for Florida vs. Texas It shouldn't be much of a surprise that none of our experts have picked the Gators, as they have lost our trust after the disastrous performances of the last two weeks. A win here would do wonders to get them back in our good graces. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. This video created with the assistance of AI. The No. 7 Longhorns (4-1, 1-1 SEC) face stumbling Florida (4-2, 2-2) Saturday morning at Royal-Memorial Stadium. With a second straight loss to the Gators, Texas would be on the verge of losing any hopes of a spot in the College Football Playoff . But a victory would right the ship for the Longhorns, especially if beleaguered quarterback Arch Manning and an error-prone special teams can trim the mistakes and play a clean game. Under first-year coach Jon Sumrall and breakout running back Jadan Baugh , Florida became one of the early-season darlings of college football after knocking off Ole Miss and climbing into the top 10 of the AP rankings. But the Gators have fallen out of the poll following two straight losses, and a porous Florida defense has given up a combined 83 points over the past two weeks to Missouri and South Carolina. Here's a full scouting report for the Texas Longhorns vs. the Florida Gators. No. 7 Texas (4-1, 1-1 SEC) vs. Florida (4-2, 2-2) When: 11 a.m. Saturday Where: Royal-Memorial Stadium TV/radio: ABC, 1300, 98.1, 105.3 (Spanish) Weather: Finally, football weather. A Friday cold front drops the temperatures near 50 degrees at kickoff and won't rise much above 70. There may be a few clouds but not much chance of rain. Texas vs Florida football betting info Moneyline: Texas -205, Florida +195 Spread: Texas is favored by 10½ points. Over/under : 52½ Texas history: Florida All-time: Texas leads 3-1-1 Last meeting: Florida 29, Texas 21 (Oct. 4, 2025) Most memorable meeting : Texas 7, Florida 7 (1924). A reported crowd of approximately 10,000 fans filled Clark Field, the current location of the Caven Lacrosse and Sports Center across San Jacinto Boulevard from Royal-Memorial Stadium. The Longhorns held on to the tie by stopping heralded Gator fullback Bill Middlekauff four times inside their own 3-yard line in the final minute of the game. MORE: 'Everything we want is is still right in front of us': Texas football eyes glimmer of hope MORE: Gators QB Aaron Philo uncertain to play due to reported injury Know the foe: Florida Last week: Lost to South Carolina, 38-19 Players to watch: RB Jadan Baugh , a 6-foot-1, 225-pound junior, serves as the centerpiece of the Gator offense. He ranks third in the SEC with 672 yards rushing and leads the conference with 12 rushing touchdowns. In two games against Texas over the past two seasons, he racked up 195 yards and two touchdowns on the ground. QB Aaron Philo , a 6-1, 207-pound junior transfer from Georgia Tech, has been solid if not spectacular, but he may miss the Texas game with an injury . He's thrown for 1,341 yards on 70.5% passing with nine touchdowns and three interceptions and has added 104 yards and three touchdowns on the ground. Edge Jayden Woods, a 6-3, 245-pound sophomore, may not quite be at the level of Texas All-American edge Colin Simmons, but he's getting closer. The twitchy pass rusher has 4 ½ sacks and six tackles for a loss, and he'll test the Longhorn pass protection. Central Texas connections: Senior TJ Shananan Jr. , a graduate of Westlake High School in Austin, has started all six games at right guard after spending two seasons at Texas A&M and one year at Penn State. Texas quarterback Arch Manning (16) runs the ball during the Red River Rivalry game against Oklahoma at the Cotton Bowl on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) When Texas has the ball This seems like a get-right game for Manning, who ranks seventh in the SEC with 224.4 yards a game on 63% passing with 10 touchdowns and five interceptions. Over the past two games against Missouri's Austin Simmons and South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers, Florida's pass defense has allowed a combined 619 yards on 70.8% passing with six touchdown passes and no interceptions. Those two quarterbacks averaged 13.5 yards per completion against the Gators, which could mean lots of action downfield for Texas receivers Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo . Will freshman Derrek Cooper get more snaps at running back for Texas? He showed flashes with a team-high 41 yards rushing against Oklahoma but averages just 3.5 yards per carry for the season. That's even lower than the Longhorns' paltry team average of 3.7 yards a carry. Buoyed by linebacker Myles Graham (41 tackles), the Gators have been respectable against the run while allowing 124.3 yards a game and 3.9 yards a carry. When Florida has the ball Florida won't shy away from the run. It ranks fifth in the SEC with 200.3 yards rushing a game and averages more than 5 yards a carry as a team. Baugh carries the load, but dynamic Duke Clark (265 yards rushing, 7.4 yards per carry) provides an intriguing change of pace. Texas allows just 96 yards rushing a game and 2.8 yards a carry, but linebackers Rasheem Biles (42 tackles) and Justin Cryer (27) are most effective using their speed to chase down backs instead of having to take on linemen. Texas outside corners Bo Mascoe and Kade Phillips have had issues this season, especially when it comes to drawing flags. Florida could test that pair as well as the rest of the secondary if healthy, but that's a big question mark entering Saturday's game. Dallas Wilson (26 catches, 376 yards, three touchdowns) had a breakout game against Texas last season. However, fellow wideout Vernell Brown III has missed the past two games with a knee injury. Brown has 17 receptions for 271 yards and two touchdowns in four games and has also returned two punts for a touchdown. Texas linebacker Rasheem Biles (3) pulls off a broken facemark after an interception during the game against Texas State at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Sep. 5, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Texas vs Florida key matchup Texas center Connor Robertson vs. Florida noseguard Brendan Bett Brendan Bett, a 6-4, 320-pound transfer from Baylor, anchors the interior of the Gators' 3-4 front from his noseguard spot. He's been active with 15 total tackles and three tackles for a loss but doesn't play at the level of the linemen from Oklahoma, Ohio State or Tennessee. If Robertson and guards Dylan Sikorski and Brandon Baker can't clear some running lanes against Bett and the Gators, they may never get the ground game going. Texas vs Florida prediction Thomas Jones: Texas 34, Florida 16. Barring any more special teams disasters or unacceptable turnovers, the Longhorns should have too much firepower for a reeling Florida defense. Danny Davis: Texas. I doubt the offense will have solved all of its problems over the past week, and don't get me started on the special teams. But only minimal improvement from Arch's bunch will be necessary if the Longhorns continue to play well against the run and subdue Jadan Baugh. Cedric Golden: Texas 27, Florida 20. The Horns respond in favorable fashion but questions remain about this offense and its inability to run the ball. Michael Shapiro: Texas 35, Florida 20. Texas coach Steve Sarkisian will get his wish for a fast start with the Longhorns back at Royal-Memorial Stadium, where they enter Saturday eyeing their 24th victory in the last 25 home games. The Longhorns are coming off one of the programs worst losses in years . And the Florida Gators are a huge reason Texas missed last year's College Football Playoff . Texas' second half collapse in the Red River Shootout last weekend has reverberated throughout college football. Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning has been a punching bag for the national media and UT haters around the nation. Texas coach Steve Sarkisian hasn't fared much better. Manning threw two catastrophic fourth quarter interceptions last Saturday against Oklahoma that has made everyone question whether he's even on the right track. And Sark's play-calling has come heavy criticism. It is almost a carbon copy of the reaction last year after the loss to Florida. If the Longhorns are going to start a redemption tour that sweeps UT into the CFP, the Gators are a good opponent to start against. Florida set the college football world on fire after upsetting Ole Miss three weeks ago. But back-to-back losses have seen the Gators come crashing back down to earth. Tommy Bresee's Prediction For Texas to keep their CFP hopes alive, this is a pseudo must-win. Florida comes with a dangerous but struggling offenses as of late. The defense is where Texas could earn a major advantage. The Gators defense has struggled mightily all season, especially defending the pass. This should be a game where Manning and the Texas offense can find a rhythm early and often. I expect Texas to begin making offensive adjustments, slow down Jadan Baugh and get the Longhorns a rather comfortable win this weekend. Final Score: Texas 34, Florida 20 Jamie Gatlin's Prediction On Saturday, the Longhorns will be looking to get back on track when they take on Florida. The Longhorns suffered their first loss of the season last week against Oklahoma due to sloppy play in the second half. To get back in the win column, Texas will have to be smart with the ball and avoid costly turnovers. They also need Arch Manning to use his legs more to open up the offense. If the Longhorns can play smarter football, then they should be able to beat a Florida team off to a 4-2 start. It will be close, but Texas should win this game. Final Score: Texas 27, Florida 20 Trey Luerssen's Prediction I think Texas wins big. The offense will click better than it has all season. Manning will look the best he has all season and the offense puts some points on the board. Defensively, Texas has another big day. Florida QB Aaron Philo is questionable, as are WRs Vernell Brown III and Bailey Stockton. The Gators will get some yards on the ground with super running back Jadan Baugh. But the passing game will be a mess. If Texas is (still) a title contender, they need to use this game as a springboard for the rest of the season. home.blurb: Texas defensive lineman Justus Terry is listed as probable. Terry has missed the past four games after suffering a toe/foot injury in warmups for the Ohio State game. He suited up last week for the Oklahoma game, but did not play. Presumably, Terry was dressed if needed in an emergency, similar to Hollywood Smothers against Tennessee. Offensive lineman Jaydon Chatman is out for the Florida game. Jordan Coleman is questionable and wide receiver Kaliq Lockett is doubtful. On the Gators side of the report, the big news is starting quarterback Aaron Philo is listed as questionable. Philo hurt his shoulder last week in a 38-19 loss to South Carolina. The Bogart, GA native has been limited in practice this week. The other two questionable players on the report are wide receivers Vernell Brown III and Bailey Stockton. Brown is reportedly trending towards playing against the Longhorns. The Gainesville native has 17 catches for 271 yards and two touchdowns through four games this season. Running back Duke Clark is listed as out. Clark has been a good compliment to star running back Jadan Baugh so far this season. Philo, who is a Georgia Tech transfer, has thrown for 1,341 yards and rushed for 104 yards so far this season. The junior has scored 12 total touchdowns with three interceptions in his first season as a starter. Stockton had his best game of the year against the Gamecocks last week. He was named the Gators Wire offensive player of the week . LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 22 LSU returns home to face No. 16 Mississippi State after last week's OT loss at Kentucky Imagn Images Jeff Lebby knows Lane Kiffin better than most. Lebby ran Kiffin's offense at Ole Miss in 2020 and 2021, and the Rebels' 2020 attack set an SEC record for total offense in conference play. Kiffin called him "a huge part of our success there" this week. Now Mississippi State's head coach, he leads the Bulldogs into a top-25 showdown with LSU on Saturday. "I don't like playing against him because they go so fast," Kiffin said this week. LSU (4-2, 1-2 SEC) is reeling after an overtime loss at Kentucky last week, and finds itself in a familiar place under previous coaches: two losses at the midpoint of the season. It wasn't supposed to start this way for Kiffin, who took over a program with deep pockets and turned the roster over into one of the most talented in the country. A third conference loss in Kiffin's first season would leave almost no margin for November, with Alabama and Texas still coming to Baton Rouge. Mississippi State (4-1, 2-1) has already won two SEC games, exceeding the one Lebby collected in his first two seasons combined. Alabama rode into Starkville and won 56-23 two weeks ago, and Kamario Taylor , the sophomore quarterback who spent September in the Heisman Trophy conversation, finished the day on the sideline with a boot on his right foot. Two weeks later, nobody outside the Bulldogs' building knows if he will play. Lebby said the SEC availability report would answer that question. LSU vs. Mississippi State: Need to know Kamario Taylor's right foot : Taylor has thrown for 1,450 yards and an SEC-best 17 touchdowns with four interceptions. He's thrown three touchdowns in the last five games, the longest stretch since LSU's Jayden Daniels in 2023. He first hurt his foot in the win over Missouri , and it showed against the Tide. He was sacked five times and finished with minus-26 rushing yards before leaving the game. If he can't play, Lebby's options are redshirt freshman Parker Puckett and AJ Swann , who spent a season at LSU. Where is Mississippi State's ground game? Fluff Bothwell has 403 yards and three touchdowns on 74 carries, but he had only one carry against Alabama and spent most of the afternoon with a boot on his left foot. The Bulldogs were outrushed 179-18. Now they get a defense that ranked second nationally against the run through four weeks, allowing 47.5 yards per game. Kentucky found cracks last week. CJ Baxter broke a 77-yard run on the first snap and finished with 123 yards. The Wildcats ran for 155 yards. The pressure is mounting in Baton Rouge as No. 22 LSU (4-2) prepares to host No. 16 Mississippi State (4-2) Saturday afternoon at Tiger Stadium. Lane Kiffin's Tigers are coming off an embarrassing 35-34 overtime loss to Kentucky, a game LSU had every opportunity to win before a questionable fourth-down decision allowed the Wildcats to force overtime. Meanwhile, Mississippi State is looking to bounce back after a disappointing loss to Alabama. With LSU already sitting at 1-2 in SEC play, another conference loss could effectively end the Tigers' College Football Playoff hopes. LSU: Can Sam Leavitt Save the Tigers? LSU's offense has shown flashes of brilliance under Kiffin, but consistency remains a major concern. Quarterback Sam Leavitt has thrown for 1,495 yards and 10 touchdowns, but his eight interceptions are the most of any quarterback in the SEC. Those turnovers have been a major issue for a team that possesses enough offensive talent to compete with nearly anyone. Running back Dilin Jones has provided stability in the backfield, rushing for 426 yards and five touchdowns through LSU's first five games. Wide receiver Winston Watkins Jr. has also emerged as a dangerous weapon, recording 354 receiving yards. Defensively, LSU has been impressive at times, particularly with edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen, who recorded eight sacks through the team's first five games. However, the Tigers just surrendered 35 points to Kentucky, raising serious questions about their ability to close out games. Against Mississippi State's explosive offense, LSU cannot afford another inconsistent defensive performance. Mississippi State: Kamario Taylor Is a PROBLEM Jeff Lebby has Mississippi State playing some exciting football, and quarterback Kamario Taylor has emerged as one of the SEC's most dangerous young players. Taylor has thrown for 1,450 yards, 17 touchdowns, and just four interceptions while completing 66.2% of his passes. However, his availability is a major concern after aggravating a lower-leg injury against Alabama. If Taylor is healthy enough to play, LSU's defense will have its hands full. Wide receiver Anthony Evans III has been outstanding, recording 40 receptions for 574 yards and five touchdowns through five games. Running back Fluff Bothwell has also been productive, rushing for 403 yards and three touchdowns while averaging 5.4 yards per carry. The Bulldogs possess enough offensive firepower to challenge LSU, but their defense remains vulnerable. Mississippi State was allowing 28 points and nearly 380 yards per game through its first five contests. That's a dangerous weakness against a Kiffin-led offense playing at home. Establishing Jones early should also create opportunities for explosive passing plays. Defensively, LSU needs to pressure Taylor if he plays and prevent Evans from creating big plays downfield. For Mississippi State, the formula revolves around attacking LSU's defense with tempo and forcing Leavitt into mistakes. If Taylor is available, his dual-threat ability could create serious problems. The Bulldogs must also establish Bothwell to prevent LSU from focusing entirely on the passing game. I expect an offensive shootout in Baton Rouge. Mississippi State has enough offensive talent to create problems for LSU, particularly if Taylor is healthy enough to play. However, I believe this is a bounce-back opportunity for Kiffin and the Tigers. Leavitt should have success attacking Mississippi State's secondary, and I expect him to throw for more than 300 yards and three touchdowns. The Bulldogs will keep things competitive throughout the afternoon, but LSU's home-field advantage and offensive firepower should ultimately make the difference. Expect Mississippi State to threaten late before LSU's defense comes up with a crucial stop to secure the victory. Lane Kiffin and his Tigers (4-2, 1-2 SEC) have suffered two losses by the midway point of the 2026 regular season, a position where no team has earned an at-large berth into the expanded, 12-team College Football Playoff field. That doesn't mean the door is 100% closed, but No. 21 LSU now has zero room for error. That feels to be a very tricky spot to be in with longtime rival No. 19 Mississippi State (4-1, 2-1) and quarterback Kamario Taylor coming to Baton Rouge for an 11 a.m. CT kickoff Saturday, Oct. 17 on ESPN. LANE KIFFIN ON KAMARIO TAYLOR Lane Kiffin calls Mississippi State QB Kamario Taylor 'a problem' SAM LEAVITT VS KENTUCKY LSU football QB Sam Leavitt said turnovers hurt Tigers vs Kentucky LSU is coming off a heartbreaking overtime loss at Kentucky, 35-34. The Bulldogs rested last week with an off week. Here's what to know about the LSU-Mississippi State pivotal SEC showdown. Mandatory Credit: Jordan Prather-Imagn Images (Jordan Prather, IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) 1 / 15 LSU football at Kentucky: Game photos from the sidelines LSU football at Kentucky: Game photos from the sidelines Kamario Taylor's health Kiffin called the Bulldogs' sophomore quarterback a "problem" earlier this week. Kiffin's Ole Miss squad saw Taylor in the regular season finale last year and he and current Ole Miss head coach, then defensive coordinator Pete Golding may still be having visions of Taylor gashing the defense. In that game, Taylor ran for 173 yards and two touchdowns. He nearly rushed for more yards than he threw for; he had 178 passing yards. Ole Miss won the game comfortably, 38-19, but as Kiffin said, Taylor has all the tools to be very problematic for defenses. Mississippi State wasn't able to firmly challenge Alabama at home two weeks ago before the off week. Taylor threw a couple of interceptions and fumbled the ball. So, turnovers were a major issues, but the dual-threat quarterback was also limited in what he could as he's been contending with a lower leg injury. It remains to be seen how healthy Taylor will be, but if he's close to 100%, or fully healthy, this game could be very interesting. Sam Leavitt turnover issues getting perfect matchup? All season to this point, LSU junior starting quarterback Sam Leavitt has had turnover problems. He's the only quarterback in college football that has thrown an interception in every game this year and his eight picks lead FBS. It's a very troubling stat and, if that trend continues, more losses are on the way for the Tigers. But is the Mississippi State defense the perfect matchup for Leavitt? Are the Bulldogs just what the doctor ordered for LSU's gunslinger? So far this season, the Bulldogs have two interceptions and their pass defense is among the worst in the SEC. Mississippi State has also only recovered two fumbles. Good news for Leavitt is Mississippi State doesn't force turnovers. Early kickoff makes LSU's matchup with Mississippi State scarier? The earliest LSU has kicked off a game in the first half of the regular season was 6 p.m. CT. And that was last week. Does that make this 11 a.m. kickoff spot scary for the Tigers welcoming in Mississippi State? The Bulldogs have only played one game so far at 11 a.m., the loss to Alabama. But it also had a 2:30 p.m. kickoff at Minnesota, which they won, 38-13. LSU practiced in the mornings during fall camp and in season. So, to Kiffin, there shouldn't been an adjustment for his team. "I think we'll play really well," Kiffin said earlier this week. "We practice in the morning every day. So they're up doing that. It's really more what their clock is. I used to be more concerned when we went to this format of the night games being opposite of their body clock. So I don't see it being an issue." LSU football offensive line play LSU struggled to find traditional balance on offense at Kentucky last week. The Wildcats don't have an awesome rush defense, but were able to keep Tiger running backs Dilin Jones and Harlem Berry from getting much of anything going. They combined for 60 rushing yards. Mississippi State's rush defense has fared better so far this season than Kentucky's has, allowing almost 16 yards on the ground less. The Bulldogs have given up five rushing scores on the season. The play up front from LSU's offense must be better this week for the team to keep the Bulldogs at bay. LSU sports the third best running attack in the SEC at 213 yards per game, but Leavitt has played a large role in that and he leads the team in rushing scores with seven. LSU's offensive line need to open run lanes for Jones and Berry against Mississippi State. LSU vs Mississippi State prediction The last time LSU lost under Kiffin a few weeks ago, it was able to bounce back at home and take care of business. Quarterback Kamario Taylor in head coach Jeff Lebby's high-flying offense poses a legit threat to any defense. And this game being an 11 a.m. kickoff also feels like a prime disaster spot for the Tigers. This game will be high scoring, but the question is: which defense will find enough stops to seal the win? I think LSU gets a couple more stops than Mississippi State's defense that averages giving up almost 40 points a game in SEC play. Be sure to check out USA TODAY Sports' new College Football Unfiltered podcast , hosted by USA TODAY Sports columnist Blake Toppmeyer. You can stream on YouTube or download via Apple podcasts and Spotify . Whether the Bulldogs will have starting quarterback Kamario Taylor under center remains uncertain. The 6-foot-4 quarterback has been one of the breakout players in the SEC through the first six weeks of the season, as he is tied for the third-most touchdown passes in the country (17) and leads the SEC with 290.0 passing yards per game. The hot start for Taylor took a bit of a halt in Week 5 vs. Alabama, as he completed a season-low 55.9% of his passes for 258 yards and three touchdowns while taking five sacks and throwing for two interceptions. Mississippi State and LSU are set for a noon ET kickoff at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge on Saturday, Oct. 17. Here's the latest on Taylor's injury: Mississippi State coach Jeff Lebby offered little clarity on the Bulldogs' quarterback situation Monday, keeping details brief when asked about the position ahead of this week's game against LSU. "Right now, the focus is getting (Taylor) ready to play and then having the ability to continue to create the depth in the room," Lebby said on Monday. "Billy (Puckett) and AJ (Swann) obviously are the two guys that have been competing since Day 1 in fall camp and really last spring. So, those guys obviously have the ability to get work if (Taylor) wasn't ready to roll." The first-year starting quarterback exited the Bulldogs' Week 5 game vs. Alabama in the fourth quarter with an apparent injury. He was seen on the ESPN broadcast first walking into the locker room with members of Mississippi State's medical staff. As noted by the Clarion Ledger — part of the USA TODAY Network — Taylor was seen wearing a boot on his right ankle for the remainder of the frame once he returned to the sidelines. Lebby noted in his postgame news conference after the 56-23 loss to Alabama that Taylor had been dealing with a prior injury heading into the game. What injury does Kamario Taylor have? Taylor is dealing with an undisclosed lower-body injury. Taylor was listed as questionable on Mississippi State's initial SEC player availability report on Wednesday for Saturday's game vs. LSU. Be sure to check out USA TODAY Sports' new College Football Unfiltered podcast , hosted by USA TODAY Sports columnist Blake Toppmeyer. You can stream on YouTube or download via Apple podcasts and Spotify . Whether the Bulldogs will have starting quarterback Kamario Taylor under center remains uncertain. The 6-foot-4 quarterback has been one of the breakout players in the SEC through the first six weeks of the season, as he is tied for the third-most touchdown passes in the country (17) and leads the SEC with 290.0 passing yards per game. The hot start for Taylor took a bit of a halt in Week 5 vs. Alabama, as he completed a season-low 55.9% of his passes for 258 yards and three touchdowns while taking five sacks and throwing for two interceptions. Mississippi State and LSU are set for a noon ET kickoff at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge on Saturday, Oct. 17. Here's the latest on Taylor's injury: Mississippi State coach Jeff Lebby offered little clarity on the Bulldogs' quarterback situation Monday, keeping details brief when asked about the position ahead of this week's game against LSU. "Right now, the focus is getting (Taylor) ready to play and then having the ability to continue to create the depth in the room," Lebby said on Monday. "Billy (Puckett) and AJ (Swann) obviously are the two guys that have been competing since Day 1 in fall camp and really last spring. So, those guys obviously have the ability to get work if (Taylor) wasn't ready to roll." The first-year starting quarterback exited the Bulldogs' Week 5 game vs. Alabama in the fourth quarter with an apparent injury. He was seen on the ESPN broadcast first walking into the locker room with members of Mississippi State's medical staff. As noted by the Clarion Ledger — part of the USA TODAY Network — Taylor was seen wearing a boot on his right ankle for the remainder of the frame once he returned to the sidelines. Lebby noted in his postgame news conference after the 56-23 loss to Alabama that Taylor had been dealing with a prior injury heading into the game. What injury does Kamario Taylor have? Taylor is dealing with an undisclosed lower-body injury. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for Georgia Football's Clash with Auburn on Saturday
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Georgia Football's Clash with Auburn on Saturday Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Georgia Bulldogs will face off against the Auburn Tigers in the Deep South’s Oldest Rivalry on Saturday afternoon. The weather forecast calls for a beautiful fall Saturday, where the high in Athens is supposed to be just 67 degrees. The betting forecast is calling for the Dawgs to beat the Tigers by about three touchdowns. This will likely not be a close game, which means we can be a little looser with our bold predictions for it. Here are three bold ones for Kirby Smart and Alex Golesh’s first game in this rivalry: Georgia has a 100-Yard Rusher and Receiver The Dawgs can take advantage of this Auburn defense, which is a bottom half unit in the conference, allowing over 350 yards of total offense per game. Georgia’s offense has been extremely productive, ranking top three in the conference. Georgia having a back and a wideout go for 100 yards in the same game hasn’t happened in 10 years. So, yeah. This is a bold prediction. I think about a guy like Talyn Taylor or Craig Dandridge, who have hit on some explosive passing plays. All it takes is one or two of those and some screens and underneath throws to work for that 100-yard game to come into play. Auburn is also among the worst rushing defenses in the SEC. We saw Dwight Phillips Jr. run for over 100 yards against Alabama on just 17 carries. He, Nate Frazier and Bo Walker have each registered multiple explosive runs. All it takes is for one of them to bust a huge run and that 100-yard mark is well within reach. Dawgs go for 250 On the Ground Auburn is allowing about 150 yards per game on the ground. I think Georgia could go for over 250. They have done it twice already and ran for over 200 yards in two other games. Auburn allowed almost 250 yards to both Tennessee and Florida. Georgia has a better offense than both of those teams. The Dawgs could really blow Auburn out on Saturday, and if they do that then there will be a lot of yards gained on the ground. Partially due to garbage time. Georgia Holds Auburn to Under 300 Total Yards Auburn has possibly the most unique offense that Georgia will see all year. There is an argument to be made that the Dawgs will struggle more in this game than you would initially think because of that. Auburn takes the least amount of time in between plays and runs more options and designed quarterback run plays than any other offense that Georgia will see this year. I am not buying it. Georgia’s defense has been the best in college football. The Dawgs will shut down Auburn on Saturday. After dominating Alabama physically, the Bulldogs could embarrass the Tigers. The Deep South's Oldest Rivalry returns to Athens this Saturday as No. 1 Georgia (6-0) welcomes Auburn (3-2) to Sanford Stadium for a 3:30 p.m. ET showdown on ESPN. And this matchup could get ugly quickly. Kirby Smart's Bulldogs are coming off an impressive 20-17 road victory over Alabama, while Auburn suffered a disappointing 24-14 loss at Tennessee. Georgia has also won nine consecutive meetings against Auburn, including last year's 20-10 victory in Jordan-Hare Stadium. Georgia: The Bulldogs Are Built DIFFERENT Georgia might have delivered its most impressive performance of the season against Alabama. Despite missing its top two running backs, Nate Frazier and Chauncey Bowens, the Bulldogs rushed for 206 yards against one of the SEC's most talented defenses. Dwight Phillips Jr. stepped up in a major way, while Bo Walker provided additional production in the backfield. Quarterback Gunner Stockton was outstanding, completing 18 of 22 passes for 249 yards while accounting for two touchdowns. Through six games, Stockton has thrown for 1,298 yards and 14 touchdowns, completing more than 76% of his passes. Defensively, Georgia held Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell to just 185 passing yards while recording four sacks. With Chris Cole, Raylen Wilson, KJ Bolden, and Ellis Robinson IV leading the defense, Georgia has the personnel to completely overwhelm Auburn's offense. Auburn: Can the Tigers Even Keep This Competitive? Auburn enters Saturday with serious questions surrounding its offense. Quarterback Byrum Brown has thrown for approximately 1,055 yards with seven touchdowns and seven interceptions. While he's dangerous with his legs, his decision-making has been inconsistent. Against Tennessee, Brown rushed for 107 yards but threw two interceptions in the 24-14 loss. Wide receiver Keshaun Singleton has emerged as a reliable target, recording 29 receptions for 322 yards. However, Auburn's biggest concern might be its inability to consistently stop the run. Tennessee rushed for 237 yards against the Tigers last weekend. That's a terrible sign considering Georgia just rushed for more than 200 yards against Alabama without its top two backs. If Auburn can't contain Georgia's rushing attack, this game could be over by halftime. How Each Team Wins For Georgia, the formula is simple: establish the running game, control the line of scrimmage, and force Brown to beat its defense through the air. Stockton should have plenty of opportunities to attack Auburn's secondary once the Tigers begin loading the box. Defensively, Georgia must contain Brown's mobility and force him into obvious passing situations. For Auburn, everything starts with avoiding turnovers and creating explosive plays. Brown must use his legs to extend drives, while the Tigers' defense needs to generate pressure on Stockton. Auburn cannot afford to fall behind early and become one-dimensional. I don't see this game being particularly competitive. Georgia is coming off an emotional victory over Alabama, but Kirby Smart has built a program that rarely overlooks inferior opponents, especially rivals. The Bulldogs should dominate the line of scrimmage, and I expect another massive rushing performance regardless of whether Frazier and Bowens return. Stockton should have an efficient afternoon, throwing multiple touchdowns while Georgia's defense forces Brown into at least two turnovers. Expect the Bulldogs to establish a commanding lead before halftime and eventually begin rotating younger players into the game. Pete Fiutak Thu, October 15, 2026 at 5:26 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads There are rivalries, and there's the Deep South's Oldest Rivalry that started in 1892 – only Minnesota vs Wisconsin has gone on longer than Auburn vs Georgia. No, it's not nearly as fierce as the Iron Bowl when Alabama takes on Auburn, but when you've played 130 times, you tend to have a few interesting moments that build into something generational. Georgia just got by Alabama in a controversial 20-17 thriller – let's just say the Bulldogs got a wee bit of a break on a key Crimson Tide deep shot – and now it's the No. 1 team in the country. Auburn has had two weeks off to get ready for this, and knocking the Bulldogs off of their lofty perch would put the first season under head coach Alex Golesh into hyperdrive. Auburn vs Georgia: Quick Hits Auburn gets LSU and the Lane Kiffin show next, and then goes to Ole Miss. Georgia gets a week off before playing the Cocktail Party showdown against Florida in Atlanta, and then it goes to Ole Miss. Georgia has won seven times in the series since losing in 2017 (it was No. 1 in the nation then, too), but it won the SEC Championship a few weeks later. The Bulldogs have won 11 of the last 12 meetings. How To Watch Auburn vs Georgia Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Sanford Stadium, Athens, GA – CFN Week 7 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Week 7 Expert Picks Why Auburn Will Win The Auburn defense has been great. It might have been hit hard by Florida, but it does a lot of bending without breaking, thanks to plenty of sacks, lots of plays behind the line, and a third down defense that's holding up well. Offensively, the high-tempo Tiger attack should be able to keep the Bulldogs on their heels. Alabama ran well last week, but it only handed the ball off 29 times. Auburn won't make that mistake, pushing for at least 35 carries, and close to 40, as it tries to hit the Georgia defense with tempo. Why Georgia Will Win Georgia's defensive front will live in the Auburn backfield. It's a problem with Auburn's style that it allows defenses to tee off on the quarterback and come up with too many tackles for loss. The Tigers don't worry about the time of possession battle, and they're good at overcoming negative plays with something positive, but Georgia has the defense to swarm all over the quick-hitting short plays. Auburn doesn't do anything deep, and Georgia should limit any yards after the catch or runs that get to the second level. Auburn vs Georgia Prediction, Betting Lines It's been an interesting start to the Golesh era. The offense is supposed to dominate and take over, but it doesn't do it enough. The defense that was so great last year has stayed strong, but it's about to get pounded on. Auburn's two losses came when it allowed over three yards per carry. Georgia is averaging over six yards per pop. picks.headline: Georgia Bulldogs vs. Auburn Tigers final score predictions: Can Alex Golesh get his first upset-rivalry win over the No. 1 team in the country?
picks.blurb: Georgia Bulldogs vs. Auburn Tigers final score predictions: Can Alex Golesh get his first upset-rivalry win over the No. 1 team in the country? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton Auburn Tigers QB Byrum Brown Randy Sartin-Imagn Images David Leong-Imagn Images Craig Smith, Justin Churchill, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness Thu, October 15, 2026 at 4:09 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Georgia Bulldogs are in a terrific spot, but they'll face one of their biggest rivals, the Auburn Tigers. The Georgia Bulldogs are the No. 1 team in the country. Auburn is a team that's trying to turn their program around. And, Alex Golesh is looking for that first unranked-upset win over a rival. Can he get it done on Saturday? A to Z Sports' experts picked the final scores for this game. Final score predictions for Georgia vs. Auburn Rob Gregson, A to Z Alabama : Georgia 30 Auburn 10 After watching the Georgia Bulldogs run all over the SEC's top-ranked rushing defense in Tuscaloosa, Auburn may be in trouble. Truthfully, Georgia is the best team in the country, and Auburn is rebuilding under first-year head coach Alex Golesh. I don't think this team has the explosiveness to score on Georgia, and they certainly don't have the physicality to win the trench battle on either side. Gunner Srockton has also elevated his game this season, making multiple high-leverage throws against Alabama in an extremely tough environment. The Dawgs will roll in this one. Tyler Forness, A to Z Florida : Georgia 45, Auburn 17 I don't see this as much of a game. The Bulldogs are coming off a big win over the Alabama Crimson Tide and showed they can hang with the best in the business. This Auburn Tigers team is in good hands with Alex Golesh, but they aren't there yet. Byrum Brown won't be able to generate much against another great Bulldogs defense. This one will likely be over at halftime. Ryan Roberts, A to Z Notre Dame : Georgia 38, Auburn 14 Georgia looks like the most complete team in the country right now, and I don't see Auburn keeping up for long in this matchup. The Bulldogs have the talent, physicality, and balance to control both sides of the ball, and I expect them to establish dominance early. Gunner Stockton is poised for a big game, taking advantage of Auburn's defense and helping Georgia put points on the board consistently. Once the Bulldogs find their offensive rhythm, the Tigers could struggle to keep this one competitive. The Georgia defense could be just as impressive. Auburn will likely have a few moments, but I don't expect the Tigers to sustain enough offense to seriously threaten the Bulldogs. Georgia can generate pressure, force mistakes, and turn defensive stops into scoring opportunities, letting the lead grow as the game progresses. This matchup highlights just how dangerous Georgia can be when all three phases click. The Bulldogs pull away comfortably and send another message to the country. Craig Smith, A to Z Tennessee : Georgia 44, Auburn 20 Boy, we've kind of forgotten about Gunner Stockton in the big picture, haven't we? The Dawgs' starting quarterback has gotten lost in the shuffle this year, with strong quarterback play from Darian Mensah, Keelon Russell, Kamario Taylor, Josh Hoover, and others. But make no mistake, he executes his team's offense as well as any signal caller in the country, as we saw in Georgia's 20-17 win over Alabama last weekend. More of the same will come on Saturday against an Auburn team that will fight for a half and then find itself out of this by the third quarter. Stockton will continue to impress, running when he needs to and spreading the ball around at a high percentage (18/22 passing last week, with completions by 10 different pass catchers). Georgia might be banged up at RB, but Dwight Phillips Jr.'s 120 yards last week against Bama proved they're basically plug-and-play in the backfield. Justin Churchill, A to Z Oklahoma : Georgia 30, Auburn 10 The Georgia Bulldogs have now proven they are the No. 1 team in the country. Their win over Alabama is about as good as it gets for any team this season, other than maybe Texas beating Ohio State. But, they have to show they can be consistent. And, there are definitely still things to work on. As for Auburn, this offense has not been as fun to watch as we all maybe thought it would in the offseason. But Georgia has the mix of defense and offense that Auburn just simply won't be able to hang around with. Then again, this is a rivalry game, and we've seen some weird things happen in rivalry games this year alone. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. picks.headline: Predictions, picks, odds for Auburn's Week 7 game at Georgia
picks.blurb: Auburn's date with Georgia will be its second of four games against a ranked team on its October schedule. The Tigers failed their first test by losing to No. 14 Tennessee in Week 5, 24-14. Auburn will also face No. 21 LSU and No. 10 Ole Miss before the calendar flips to November. Georgia handled its first true test last Saturday, defeating No. 6 Alabama on the road, 20-17. The Bulldogs outgained Alabama, 455-346, but struggled in the penalty department, committing seven for 57 yards. The win, in addition to Texas' loss to unranked Oklahoma, pushed Georgia to the No. 1 spot in both the US LBM Coaches Poll and the Associated Press poll ahead of Week 7. The Bulldogs are the nation's No. 1 team for several reasons, most of which can be found in stats. Georgia ranks No. 2 nationally in points per game (46.2), and is No. 1 in the SEC in points allowed (14.0), which ranks No. 11 nationally. Georgia also produces 474.8 yards per game while allowing opponents to gain 261.5 per game. Georgia is also great at protecting quarterback Gunner Stockton as they have allowed only six sacks through the midway point of the regular season. Auburn is in the lower-tier of most SEC stat categories, but is among the conference's best in interceptions. Auburn has hauled in six interceptions this season, which is tied with LSU and Missouri for the third-most in the SEC. away.headline: Georgia football injury report: Key Georgia defender questionable for Auburn
away.blurb: Per the SEC’s Availability Report, Nate Frazier is expected to be available for Georgia’s game against Auburn on Saturday, but junior safety KJ Bolden is questionable. He’s one of six Bulldogs listed on the report , which was released Wednesday night. Georgia has already ruled out junior wideout Isiah Canion, sophomore wideout Thomas Blackshear, junior running back Chauncey Bowens, junior EDGE Amaris Williams and freshman defensive back Tyriq Green. Junior offensive lineman Marcus Harrison, who has missed the past four games, is considered probable. With Canion out, Blackshear had taken on a bigger role, that was until he suffered a collarbone injury in the Vanderbilt game. The Savannah native caught three passes for 33 yards before leaving the game. Blackshear started his first game in Week 4 vs. Oklahoma. Green should be nearing a return after suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 2. Green suffered the injury shortly after returning a 93-yard kickoff for a touchdown. He underwent tightrope surgery, but Georgia has no need to rush him back. Green was the Bulldogs’ top kick returner through the first two games. After suffering a torn ACL in spring drills, Williams is likely out for the entire regular season. However, he could return for the postseason. Bowens had Lisfranc surgery and is likely done for the rest of the season. He sustained that injury in Georgia’s win over Vanderbilt in Week 5. Frazier, who hasn’t played since Week 3 against Arkansas, is not listed at all. Bolden is a new addition, but he’s battling a lower-body injury. Canion is in line to miss his fourth straight game with a bone bruise in his knee. He traveled to Arkansas last month as Georgia opened SEC play and got the start. He left that game in the opening series after aggravating the injury. The former Georgia Tech standout hasn’t played since.

home.blurb: Why Georgia has an advantage: Auburn quarterback Byrum Brown ranks 14th in the SEC in passing efficiency and has as many interceptions as touchdowns with 7 each. Auburn is 81st against the run nationally at 149 yards per game and gave up touchdown runs of 25 and 44 in its last game at Tennessee. “This team, man, are you going to take this and grow from it?” Smart said. “The naysayers said they couldn’t go there and win and they ain’t played nobody.” Alabama certainly was a step up in competition, a team the Bulldogs traded haymakers with all night in a 20-17 victory. The challenge for Georgia (6-0, 4-0 SEC) this week is to turn the page from an opponent that now feels like a rivalry to many to one that has been one of the biggest and is its longest in Auburn . This is the 131 st meeting between the schools some 180 miles apart. Auburn (4-2, 1-2) will have a fourth different head coach on the sideline since Smart came aboard in Athens. Smart has gone up against Gus Malzahn, Bryan Harsin, Hugh Freeze and now will face Alex Golesh. The Tigers are ranked No. 33 on ESPN’s SP+, which puts it 11 th in the SEC and below an Oklahoma team that Georgia rolled past three weeks ago. The Tigers had an open date on their schedule last week, giving the players a break from the grind and coaches more of a chance to evaluate how to get better. “They're coming off an off week, and we're coming off a really tough physical game,” Smart said. “It will be really important that the mindset and the approach to the game is right because they want to make it physical the way they play.” Georgia is No. 1 ranked for the first time since September of 2024. It moved to that spot a day after top-ranked Texas was upset by unranked Oklahoma. Two other top 15 SEC teams also went down to unranked foes: No. 10 LSU to Kentucky and No. 15 Florida to South Carolina. Smart alluded to those results when talking about the challenge Auburn presents. “They have a lot of talent,” Smart said. “They've got good football players, and it's any given Saturday in this conference, as we see every week.” Auburn is missing perhaps its most valuable piece. home.headline: Georgia football injury report: Key Georgia defender questionable for Auburn
home.blurb: Per the SEC’s Availability Report, Nate Frazier is expected to be available for Georgia’s game against Auburn on Saturday, but junior safety KJ Bolden is questionable. He’s one of six Bulldogs listed on the report , which was released Wednesday night. Georgia has already ruled out junior wideout Isiah Canion, sophomore wideout Thomas Blackshear, junior running back Chauncey Bowens, junior EDGE Amaris Williams and freshman defensive back Tyriq Green. Junior offensive lineman Marcus Harrison, who has missed the past four games, is considered probable. With Canion out, Blackshear had taken on a bigger role, that was until he suffered a collarbone injury in the Vanderbilt game. The Savannah native caught three passes for 33 yards before leaving the game. Blackshear started his first game in Week 4 vs. Oklahoma. Green should be nearing a return after suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 2. Green suffered the injury shortly after returning a 93-yard kickoff for a touchdown. He underwent tightrope surgery, but Georgia has no need to rush him back. Green was the Bulldogs’ top kick returner through the first two games. After suffering a torn ACL in spring drills, Williams is likely out for the entire regular season. However, he could return for the postseason. Bowens had Lisfranc surgery and is likely done for the rest of the season. He sustained that injury in Georgia’s win over Vanderbilt in Week 5. Frazier, who hasn’t played since Week 3 against Arkansas, is not listed at all. Bolden is a new addition, but he’s battling a lower-body injury. Canion is in line to miss his fourth straight game with a bone bruise in his knee. He traveled to Arkansas last month as Georgia opened SEC play and got the start. He left that game in the opening series after aggravating the injury. The former Georgia Tech standout hasn’t played since.

home.headline: Auburn vs. Georgia early injury report: Who's in, who's out
home.blurb: The Tigers emerge from the bye week relatively healthy, with only two players, tight end Hunter Herring and offensive lineman Tai Buster, ruled out for Saturday's game at Georgia due to injury. However, the biggest news from the initial report is that linebacker Xavier Atkins is officially ruled out. Auburn Tigers — OUT: LB Xavier Atkins, TE Hunter Herring, OL Tai Buster Georgia Bulldogs — OUT: WR Thomas Blackshear, RB Chauncey Bowens, WR Isiah Canion, LB Amaris Williams, S Tyriq Green; Questionable: DB KJ Bolden; Probable: OL Marcus Harrison Atkins, who is tied for the team lead in sacks and second on the team in tackles, has been suspended for Saturday's game at No. 1 Georgia, according to Auburn head coach Alex Golesh. Golesh first mentioned the suspension during Monday's press conference and clarified Wednesday that Atkins is not with the team during practice this week. Golesh will address Atkins' status again next week. The Bulldogs will be without several players, including running back Chauncey Bowens, who leads the team in rushing touchdowns with six. However, Georgia received potentially good news on Wednesday as running back Nate Frazier is not on the availability report after missing four straight games with a rib injury. He was not included on the availability report for Georgia's Week 6 game at Alabama ; however, he did not play.
