LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 6 Alabama looks to recover from its first loss of the season on Saturday at No. 14 Tennessee Getty Images A pair of historic rivals with playoff aspirations are squaring off in a top-15 SEC showdown on Saturday, as No. 6 Alabama travels to No. 14 Tennessee for the Third Saturday in October. The Crimson Tide will be looking to avoid losing consecutive regular season games for the first time since 2007, while the Volunteers will be seeking to snap a four-game home losing streak against ranked opponents. Alabama (5-1, 3-1 SEC) took a 20-17 home loss to Georgia last week, which leaves the Crimson Tide with a dwindling margin for error entering the second half of their schedule. Tennessee (5-1, 2-1) is coming off an ugly 24-17 win at Arkansas in need of the resume boost that would come with knocking off Alabama. While Tennessee's defense is thriving midway through the season, facing Alabama will be its toughest test yet. Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell leads the league in passing yards with 1,599 and brings game-changing mobility. Though Alabama star receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams is expected to miss the game due to injury, Bama's offense will still pack a punch that tests Tennessee's secondary. The Volunteers counter with the nation's No. 15 rushing offense and a languishing passing attack that will need to get better if they are going to pull an upset that would reverberate through the SEC and beyond. With blowout road wins over quality foes Kentucky and Mississippi State already in hand, the Tide will look to keep rolling on the road with their first win in Knoxville since 2020. Alabama vs. Tennessee: Need to know Neyland blues: The last time Tennessee beat a ranked team at Neyland Stadium was in 2024, when it edged No. 7 Alabama 24-17. The Vols finished 0-3 at home against ranked opponents last season and fell 20-17 to Texas in Week 4, extending their home losing streak against ranked opponents to four games. But something will have to give as the Crimson Tide have dropped two straight inside Neyland Stadium. Whichever team is smoking, the traditional postgame victory cigars will hit a little different this time. Tennessee's QB question: Tennessee sophomore quarterback George MacIntyre made his first career start last week in the Volunteers' 24-17 win at Arkansas, stepping in for injured and underperforming freshman Faizon Brandon . Now the question is how long the Volunteers will stick with MacIntyre, who completed 18 of 29 passes for 247 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions against the Razorbacks. Regardless of who gets the nod against Alabama, the Crimson Tide's priority will be to slow down the SEC's second-leading rusher, DeSean Bishop , and to make Tennessee's fledgling passing attack prove that it can deliver. Playoff implications: With a win, Alabama will have an 87.7% chance of reaching the College Football Playoff, according to the CBS Sports College Football Playoff Forecaster. A loss would drop that mark to 52.9% and crush Alabama's margin for error. Because the Crimson Tide's strength of schedule lags behind others in the SEC, its case for inclusion as a three-loss team would be shaky. Tennessee's playoff odds would shoot to 51.6% with a win and drop to 16.8% with a loss. Where to watch Alabama vs. Tennessee live Date : Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Neyland Stadium -- Knoxville, Tennessee TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Alabama vs. Tennessee prediction, picks Tennessee's defense and run game have carried it to a 5-1 start. Replicating that formula against Alabama won't be possible unless the Crimson Tide shoot themselves in the foot with turnovers and special team miscues. Because the Crimson Tide won't respect the Volunteers' passing game, they'll be able to load the box and frustrate Tennessee's ground game, much like Texas did in Week 4. Offensively, Alabama has too much firepower to be fully restrained for four quarters. Look for Bama to pull away in the fourth quarter. On the "Third Saturday in October," Tennessee hosts Alabama at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn., as the Volunteers look to win against their rival for the third time in five years. The Crimson Tide are 7.5-point road favorites, and my Alabama vs. Tennessee prediction and college football picks expect Kalen DeBoer to continue Nick Saban's tradition of blowing out the Vols. TOP PICK Who will win Alabama vs Tennessee: Alabama -7.5 If last week was any indicator, Tennessee has far more problems than Alabama , despite the Volunteers' win and the Crimson Tide's loss. In George MacIntyre's first start for Josh Heupel, he finished with just a 10.3 QBR in a seven-point win against Arkansas. He'll be starting again against Bama, which is why I like the Tide to cover -9.5 or better . Arkansas lost to its previous three Power Four opponents by an average of 29.3 points, including a 28-point defeat to Georgia — the same team Alabama lost to by just three on the road last week. Tennessee's offense won't be able to keep up with Alabama. Keelon Russell ranks third nationally in QBR (90.0) , and the Tide are top 20 in offensive success rate (50.1%). The Alabama vs. Tennessee rivalry history is full of winning streaks, and this could be the start of another. Alabama vs Tennessee Over/Under pick: Over 50.5 For this Over to hit (I'd take it at 51.5 or better ), Alabama will need to do the bulk of the scoring, and the Tide will push for 31+ points given Russell's recent play. The former five-star recruit has put up an 8 0.9+ QBR in four straight games while accounting for 14 TDs. His dual-threat ability has helped open up the run game, too, with Alabama ranking fourth nationally in rush success rate (53.3%) . That will force Jim Knowles' defense to stay honest instead of solely focusing on protecting the back end. Meanwhile, Tennessee should be able to put up 20+ points to help push the total Over. The Volunteers have one of the best run games in the country (No. 2 in EPA per rush), led by DeSean Bishop . Bishop ranks top 10 nationally in rushing yards after contact (465). Alabama vs Tennessee combo One word describes Tennessee's passing game: rocky. The Volunteers are 128th nationally in pass success rate (33.8) , and MacIntyre has a QBR of 24.7 this season. That won't cut it against an Alabama defense tied for the 14th-most sacks in the country (17). I'm expecting a fast start from Russell after last week's tough loss to Georgia, and once Bama takes the lead, Tennessee isn't equipped to come back with MacIntyre behind center. The Tide, who are ninth nationally on defense in rush success rate (35.4%), should be able to focus on slowing Bishop enough to win by 10+ points. The latest chapter in the storied Third Saturday in October rivalry, Alabama has dropped their last two games played in Neyland Stadium, and will face yet another significant challenge Saturday afternoon. Tennessee sits at 5-1 overall (2-1 SEC), and are currently ranked as the nation's No. 14 team in the latest US LBM Coaches Poll . A matchup that is loaded with potential storylines , following is a look at three predictions for Saturday's showdown in Knoxville between the Crimson Tide and Volunteers. Alabama defense forces three Tennessee turnovers Oct 10, 2026; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide defensive back Bray Hubbard (18) celebrates his interception during the second quarter against the Georgia Bulldogs at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images According to ESPN's Pete Thamel , Alabama's defense will be facing George MacIntyre at quarterback for Tennessee on Saturday afternoon, a sophomore who will be making only his second-career start. MacIntyre, who had two picks a week ago against Arkansas, will be facing an Alabama defense that leads the SEC with nine interceptions this year, and I'll predict to add at-least two to that total Saturday afternoon, if not more. Noah Rogers has breakout performance Oct 3, 2026; Starkville, Mississippi, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide wide receiver Noah Rogers (5) runs after a catch during the fourth quarter against the Mississippi State Bulldogs at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Alabama wide receiver Noah Rogers has played in three games since returning from an offseason injury, but has yet to fully breakout for the Crimson Tide having made only three catches for 55 yards. With the Crimson Tide's leading receiver, Ryan Coleman-Williams, set to miss Saturday's game , Alabama will certainly need someone at the position to step up, and I'll say Rogers does exactly that with his best performance since arriving in Tuscaloosa. Alabama offensive line bounces back with big showing Oct 3, 2026; Starkville, Mississippi, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide offensive lineman Jackson Lloyd (77) lines up during the fourth quarter against the Mississippi State Bulldogs at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Alabama's offensive line, which allowed four sacks a week ago against Georgia, faces a significant test in Knoxville this Saturday in a Tennessee defense that is currently leading the nation with 25 sacks on the season. Despite the unit facing an unknown surrounding the status of starting center Racin Delgatty, I'll still predict a bounce back from the Crimson Tide's offensive front in not only pass protection, but also helping pave the way for a big showing on the Alabama run game. Nearly everyone in and around college football will be keeping a close eye on this weekend's matchup between Alabama and Tennessee. The Vols are set to host the Crimson Tide in a game that will put the winner on a clear path to the College Football Playoff (both teams are currently 5-1). Tennessee has won the last two matchups in Knoxville. Former Oklahoma head coach Bob Stoops predicts winner of Alabama vs Tennessee Former Oklahoma head coach Bob Stoops made his picks for this weekend's biggest games. And he has Alabama getting the win over Tennessee on Saturday in Neyland Stadium. "They've looked really strong," said Stoops of Alabama. "I'm going to take Alabama. Tennessee's been winning by one score and been in tighter games. Alabama, coming off that Georgia game, will have something to prove. So I'll take Alabama." Stoops, by the way, has nailed his last two predictions for Alabama vs Tennessee. He had the Vols winning at home in 2024 and then he picked Alabama to win in Tuscaloosa last season . Tennessee and Alabama are set to kick off at 3:30 PM ET on Saturday. The game will air on ABC. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. On the other side of the ball, UA’s defensive line was already depleted with Jeremiah Beaman out. On Saturday, Terrance Green reaggravated a previous injury, and will miss the Tennessee matchup. away.headline: Alabama dealt unfortunate injury news ahead of Tennessee clash
away.blurb: The Alabama Crimson Tide will look to bounce back after a razor close loss to the Georgia Bulldogs in Week 6 when they face off against the Tennessee Volunteers. But unfortunately, they will not be at full strength offensively in Saturday’s game. Junior wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams has been one of the more reliable and effective wide receivers in all of college football this season for the Crimson Tide. Prior to their loss to Georgia, Coleman-Williams had put together a three-game streak of finding the end zone at least once. During their Week 6 loss to Georgia, Coleman-Williams was forced to exit the game after both seemingly re-aggravating a knee injury in the game and suffering a concussion, which was what ultimately cut his game in Week 6 short. More news : Mississippi State QB Kamario Taylor Vows to ‘Ruin’ LSU’s Night Leading up to the team’s Week 7 game, there was not much optimism that Coleman-Williams was going to be able to suit up for the game. And that reality was confirmed on Wednesday when Alabama released their weekly injury report, along with a report on the matter from Pete Nakos of On3 Sports. More news : UCLA HC Bob Chesney Drops Powerful Quote After Bruins’ Hot Start Considering Coleman-Williams leads the team in every major statistical category, including receptions (tied with Lotzeir Brooks), receiving yards, and receiving touchdowns, his absence on Saturday will almost certainly be missed. Add in the fact that the Tennessee Volunteers allow just 161.3 passing yards per game to opposing teams, the second-lowest passing yards allowed to opponents in the SEC, and it could very well be a tough day for Alabama star quarterback Keelon Russell. Saturday’s Alabama-Tennessee matchup will kick off at 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC. home.blurb: UA’s starting center, Delgatty was listed as doubtful on Thursday’s availability report. If he can’t go, Mal Waldrep is set to step in at center, after he took over for his injured teammate against Georgia. On the other side of the ball, UA’s defensive line was already depleted with Jeremiah Beaman out. On Saturday, Terrance Green reaggravated a previous injury, and will miss the Tennessee matchup. Early in the week it became clear that one of Alabama’s top playmakers was going to miss the trip to Knoxville. Ryan Coleman-Williams was already dealing with injuries before taking a head-to-head hit against Georgia, and was declared out on the first availability report of the week. “We learn from this week and we go bring the same energy we had last Tuesday, the Tuesday before that and the excitement and understanding that we get to go do this. Like, this is what you wanted. This is what you came here for. Let’s make the most of them. Take advantage of the opportunity to go out there and play in an awesome environment that’s going to be there on Saturday, and now we just gotta go prepare for it.” One week after a tough loss to Georgia, Alabama football returns to SEC play on Saturday. The Crimson Tide faces a tough trip to Tennessee , with both teams entering the game with 5-1 records. The game is scheduled to kick off at 2:30 p.m. CT Saturday at Neyland Stadium. Before the Third Saturday in October game, here are three questions for Alabama to answer. Can the Crimson Tide overcome injuries up front? On offense, it was Racin Delgatty who went down, with a lower leg injury. The Crimson Tide will need to hope for no further injuries up front. home.blurb: News Sports Counties Business Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL Key Alabama starters listed as 'out' vs. Tennessee in Week 7 Matt Melton Roll Tide Wire Oct. 15, 2026, 8:01 a.m. CT According to the SEC's initial Week 7 Availability Report revealed Wednesday night, a pair of key Alabama starters have been officially listed as "out" for Saturday's game at Tennessee. In addition to those two, Alabama starting center Racin Delgatty has also been listed as "questionable," while Justin Hill, an outside linebacker, carries a "probable" tag. Delgatty also exited the Georgia game with injury, while Hill is a potential big boost for the Crimson Tide defense, as the talented edge rusher has not played since the Florida State game. For Tennessee, the biggest injury to monitor leading up to Saturday is starting quarterback Faizon Brandon, who is listed as "questionable." If the true freshman is unable to go, George MacIntyre would get the start. Both of Coleman-Williams and Green exited the Georgia game with injuries, with Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer stating earlier in the week that both have been dealing with lingering issues. Over six games this season, Coleman-Williams is Alabama's leading receiver with 23 receptions for 415 yards and four touchdowns, as well as the Crimson Tide 's primary punt returner. Green starts for the Crimson Tide inside at defensive tackle where he has 11 tackles, four TFL, and 2.5 sacks, and is one of Alabama's top linemen against the run. picks.headline: Ole Miss vs Missouri Predictions: Who Wins Critical Matchup and Why?
picks.blurb: Ole Miss vs Missouri Predictions: Who Wins Critical Matchup and Why? Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS Somewhat quietly, one of the bigger games on college football slate this weekend is happening at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium between No. 9 Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1 SEC) and No. 13 Missouri (5-1, 2-1 SEC). Both squads enter with one loss and need a win this weekend to maintain a reasonable path to the College Football Playoffs. However, alongside the high-stakes of the matchup are the storylines revolving around each team’s roster. Rebels’ star running back Kewan Lacy will be facing his former team for the first time since leaving Missouri, following his true freshman season in 2024. Meanwhile, former Ole Miss starters Austin Simmons, Cayden Lee and Chris Graves Jr. all return to Oxford for the first time since they entered the transfer portal, following the Rebels’ deep run through last year’s playoffs. Saturday’s kickoff between the Rebels and Tigers is set for 2:30 p.m. CT on the SEC Network. Ole Miss entered the week as six-point home favorites. Ahead of the Rebels' latest pressure-filled matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Sep 26, 2026; Gainesville, Florida, USA; Mississippi Rebels head coach Pete Golding looks on after an interception against the Florida Gators during the second half at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tyler Komis Welcome to the gauntlet that is the College Football Playoffs….or at least the very real warmup version of it. The loser of this weekend’s game in Oxford isn’t mathematically out of the 12-team race, but it’s going to be a loss that will be immensely hard to overcome looking at Ole Miss’ and Missouri’s schedule. As far as the actual matchup is concerned, going into the game, Missouri has played better on the defensive side of the ball and matches the Rebels’ offensive firepower with Austin Simmons and Jamal Roberts leading the way. The Tigers’ rush attack could have the ability to give the Rebels a long afternoon, and we’ll really find out if Ole Miss improved enough from its nightmare performance defending the run against Florida. Ole Miss doesn’t have to completely shut down Mizzou’s ground game, it more than likely won’t, but if it can limit Roberts and the rest of the production in the backfield, the Rebels should give themselves a real chance at picking up a critical win. In my mind, that’s going to be the key to victory for Ole Miss. I believe this game will come down to the final few possessions and whichever offense has the ball last in that scenario. Given the large sample size we’ve seen of Trinidad Chambliss in those types of situations, I have a hard time picking against those results. Ole Miss 34, Missouri 31 Matt Galatzan All of the talk is going to be about the return of Austin Simmons and Cayden Lee to Oxford, and Kewan Lacy facing off against his former team. However, there needs to be more talk about Missouri's defense, or more specifically, its pass rush. The Tigers have 18 sacks this year, which is tied with Texas for third in the SEC behind LSU and Tennessee. Meanwhile, the Rebels are No. 1 in the SEC in sacks allowed with just five. If the Rebels can protect Trinidad Chambliss and slow down a balanced Missouri offense, they will be in good shape. I think they do both just enough to get the win. Ole Miss 30, Missouri 27 I think Ole Miss will take home a hard-fought victory against former Rebels’ quarterback Austin Simmons, wide receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. and the rest of the Missouri Tigers. Simmons, Lee and running back Jamal Roberts are likely to give head coach Pete Golding and his defense trouble, leading to a “bend-don’t-break” type of performance, following a bounce-back game against Vanderbilt for the Rebels’ defense. However, I’m comfortable predicting Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, wide receiver Deuce Alexander and running back Kewan Lacy to outplay Simmons, Lee and Roberts and give the Rebels a high-scoring ranked win in Ole Miss’ homecoming game. Ole Miss 38, Missouri 31 Zion Trammell Ole Miss and Missouri feature star-studded quarterbacks in Trinidad Chambliss and Austin Simmons. This has the makings of a high-scoring affair, so whichever quarterback can protect the ball better could decide the outcome. I think Chambliss and Kewan Lacy play their best games of the year, and Ole Miss gets by with a win. Ole Miss 31, Missouri 28 Cooper Ferguson Back in the Vaught, I want to see a great response to the blowout victory in Nashville. All will go well if Trinidad Chambliss plays as he has so far. After a second-half respite in the Vanderbilt game, Kewan Lacy is primed for a breakout game in the 2026 campaign. I fear the talent and connection between Austin Simmons and Cayden Lee, but I do not see the Rebels dropping a game at VHS this season. He is a Biletnikoff Award and Lombardi Award voter from New Jersey with more than five years of sports reporting experience. Heisman contender Trinidad Chambliss has propelled Ole Miss to a 4-1 SU start to the season, including wins over No. 24 Louisville and No. 7 LSU . The Rebels were blown out by the Gators in an emotional letdown spot after getting revenge on Lane Kiffin, who left Ole Miss prior to the team's appearance in last year's College Football Playoff to take more money at LSU. Other than that, Ole Miss has looked like one of the best teams in the nation. In Week 6, Ole Miss scored a touchdown on four of its first five possessions against Vanderbilt — a team that held Auburn to 21 points and gave Georgia its t oughest test of the season. The market is showing Missouri a lot of respect following consecutive blowout wins against Florida and Texas A&M, but both of those games were played at home. In its only road matchup against a ranked opponent, Missouri allowed 31 points and 499 yards of total offense to Mississippi State . Missouri was also on upset alert earlier this fall in a road game at Kansas, which was tied 14-14 at the half before the Jayhawks turned the ball over on each of their first two possessions of the third quarter. Traders should not disregard Missouri's early-season road struggles. They also shouldn't overlook how much this game means for the Rebels, who haven't defeated the Tigers in a football game since 1974. Home-field advantage and a little extra motivation to end a historic losing streak could be deciding factors in Ole Miss successfully covering. Can the Tigers pull off another upset, or will the Rebels defend Oxford? Two of the SEC's most intriguing teams are set to collide Saturday afternoon as No. 13 Missouri (5-1) travels to Oxford to face No. 9 Ole Miss (4-1). Both programs are coming off dominant victories. Missouri dismantled Texas A&M 27-6, while Ole Miss embarrassed Vanderbilt 52-17. With both teams sitting at 2-1 in conference play, Saturday's matchup could have major implications for the SEC Championship race and College Football Playoff. Missouri: The Tigers Are Legitimate Contenders Eli Drinkwitz has Missouri playing some outstanding football, particularly on defense. The Tigers are allowing just 17.7 points per game and rank eighth nationally in rushing defense, surrendering approximately 78 yards per contest. Offensively, former Ole Miss quarterback Austin Simmons has thrown for 1,434 yards, 14 touchdowns, and just one interception. Now, he gets an opportunity to prove himself against his former program. But Missouri's biggest weapon has been running back Jamal Roberts. Roberts has rushed for 828 yards and eight touchdowns, including consecutive 200-yard performances. Against an Ole Miss defense allowing 176.4 rushing yards per game, he could be in for another massive afternoon. Former Ole Miss wide receiver Cayden Lee has also been outstanding, recording 42 receptions for 616 yards and five touchdowns. If Missouri establishes its rushing attack early, the Tigers could control this game. Ole Miss: Can Trinidad Chambliss Carry the Rebels? Pete Golding has Ole Miss back in the national conversation following last season's historic playoff run. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss continues to be one of the most exciting players in college football, throwing for 1,435 yards and 11 touchdowns through five games. Wide receiver Deuce Alexander has emerged as his favorite target, recording 32 receptions for 503 yards and five touchdowns. The Rebels are averaging 38.8 points and nearly 434 yards per game, but their defense remains a major concern. Ole Miss is allowing 28 points per game, including an embarrassing 52-point performance against Florida earlier this season. And facing Missouri's balanced offense certainly won't make things easier. However, the Rebels have been outstanding at home, winning all three of their games in Oxford this season. How Each Team Wins Missouri must establish Roberts early and force Ole Miss into a physical, defensive battle. If the Tigers can dominate time of possession and limit explosive plays from Chambliss, they have an excellent opportunity to leave Oxford with a victory. For Ole Miss, everything starts with its passing attack. Missouri's defense has been elite against the run, meaning Chambliss will likely need to carry the offense. The Rebels must also force Simmons into mistakes and prevent Roberts from consistently reaching the second level. This matchup has all the ingredients for one of the best SEC games of the weekend. Missouri's rushing attack should give the Rebels serious problems, and I expect Roberts to surpass 100 yards once again. However, I trust Chambliss and the Ole Miss offense to deliver when it matters most. The Rebels' explosive passing attack, combined with a sold-out Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, should be enough to overcome Missouri's physicality. Expect a back-and-forth contest that comes down to the final minutes, with Chambliss engineering a late scoring drive to secure the victory. away.blurb: Simmons, top receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. weren’t made available to speak Tuesday about transferring from Ole Miss, but it’s worth noting that Simmons’ Instagram account still has a number of posts from his years in Oxford. “I feel like those guys are definitely going to come out and play with a chip on their shoulder,” tailback Jamal Roberts said. “We definitely can let them guys handle that.” No. 9 Ole Miss reached the College Football Playoff semifinals a season ago with Trinidad Chambliss at quarterback after Simmons went down early with an injury and lost his starting job. Tigers coach Eli Drinkwitz acknowledged that the game will be a big deal for Simmons, along with two other Mizzou players imported from Ole Miss. Drinkwitz just wants them to keep perspective, considering about 20% of FBS players are transfers. “The biggest thing is to not make it bigger than it is,” Drinkwitz told reporters Tuesday. “There are great memories from there. I think everybody left there in a positive light on both sides.” “We talk about the joy of the journey,” Drinkwitz said. “That was a part of their journey that made them who they are right now. I don’t think there has to be a whole lot more to it than that.” Mizzou (5-1, 2-1 Southeastern Conference) comes in having won two straight home games against SEC foes, most recently 27-6 over Texas A&M on Saturday. Roberts will be another focal point for Ole Miss. After putting together two straight games of 200-plus yards, he ranks first in the SEC and second nationally with 828 rushing yards. Mizzou’s top back a season ago, Ahmad Hardy, is recovering from an offseason gunshot wound. Golding said that Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1 SEC) will have its hands full trying to tackle Roberts. “He has the most yards after contact right now, which is something that has been an issue for us on tape,” Golding said. home.blurb: THURSDAY Ole Miss vs. Missouri Injury Report: Safety MJ Preston Upgraded to Probable, Former Rebel Cayden Lee Also Probable ‘I've got to go out there and earn it’: Hunter Elliott returns with something to prove as Ole Miss opens fall OXFORD, Miss. – Ole Miss safety MJ Preston has been upgraded from questionable to probable ahead of Saturday's game between No. 9 Ole Miss and No. 13 Missouri, according to the SEC's second availability report released at 7:10 p.m. CT Thursday. For Missouri, former Ole Miss wide receiver Cayden Lee was also upgraded from questionable to probable, and former Rebels quarterback Austin Simmons remains probable. The Rebels list nine players as out, while Missouri lists six out and two doubtful. Safety Edwin Joseph remains out after undergoing a tightrope procedure on his ankle . Ole Miss: Offensive lineman Enoch Wangoy (No. 77) moved from questionable to out. Safety MJ Preston (No. 19) was upgraded from questionable to probable. Tight end Hayden Bradley (No. 80) remains questionable. Missouri: Wide receiver Cayden Lee (No. 19) was upgraded from questionable to probable. Offensive lineman Khalief Canty Jr. (No. 58) moved from questionable to out. Linebacker Jeremiah Beasley (No. 6) and tight end Brett Norfleet (No. 87) moved from questionable to doubtful. Safety Santana Banner (No. 15), edge Darris Smith (No. 19), cornerback Cameron Keys (No. 20) and offensive lineman Cayden Green (No. 70) were upgraded from questionable to probable. Missouri wide receiver Shaun Terry II, who was questionable Wednesday, is no longer on the report. Six Tigers who were listed as probable Wednesday are also off the list: DaMarion Fowlkes, Nicholas Rodriguez, Kensley Louidor-Faustin, Langden Kitchen, Jayden McGregory and Jordon Harris. The only change to the Ole Miss out list is Wangoy, a transfer from Florida. Preston's upgrade gives the Rebels another option at safety with Joseph sidelined. The biggest news for the Tigers is Lee. He leads Missouri with 42 catches for 616 yards and five touchdowns, and the upgrade means Simmons is likely to have his top target available in Oxford. Running back Ahmad Hardy remains out. Missouri trended healthier on Thursday, and the Lee upgrade is the change that matters most for the Ole Miss secondary. With Joseph out, the Rebels will need Nick Cull at nickel and safeties Ladarian Clardy and MJ Preston ready to handle a passing game built around Simmons and Lee. Robert Woodyard Jr., Missouri's third-leading tackler with 44 stops and an interception, remains questionable and is the Tigers' most important name to watch on Friday's report. home.blurb: Three former Ole Miss players will return to Oxford on Saturday as Missouri Tigers, just six games and less than ten months after leaving the Rebels in the transfer portal. Despite the unique situation, head coach Eli Drinkwitz said that the game is about much more than the return and should be, instead, a testament to what the Tigers have done this season. Missouri has a lengthy injury report as of Thursday night, which is very similar to their report against Texas A&M. Despite having 11 players listed as questionable or probable against the Aggies, they all were available come game time. Against Ole Miss, the Tigers have two doubtful players in Jeremiah Beasley and Brett Norfleet and two questionable players in Roberty Woodyard Jr. and Sterling Webb. There are also seven probable Missouri players: Austin Simmons, Cayden Lee, Cayden Green, Daeden Hopkins, Darris Smith, Santana Banner and Cameron Keys. Missouri has six officially sidelined Tigers, with the most prominent being Ahmad Hardy. Cornerback Antonio Kite was another notable player on the injury report, listed as probable. Kite has one of four Ole Miss interceptions on the season. As a whole, Ole Miss has nine players out, one questionable and three probable, most of which are reserves. Following a strong 2025 Ole Miss campaign, wide receiver Cayden Lee, cornerback Chris Graves Jr. and quarterback Austin Simmons all entered the transfer portal and chose to join a conference foe in the Missouri Tigers. Since joining, the three transfers are now starters in Columbia, and Simmons and Lee have become stars, ranking top five in multiple SEC categories. "There's going to be a lot made about Cayden and Austin and CG going back, but really it's more about our team playing well and the opportunity that we've created for ourselves being in a top-15 matchup," Drinkwitz said in a press conference on Tuesday. Drinkwitz mentioned that in two of the Tigers' six games, previous players or coaches matched up against their old teams, explaining that it's the "new age of college football." In the Week 7 matchup between No. 13 Missouri and No. 9 Ole Miss that statement is even more applicable, as the Rebels also have three former Missouri players and coaches on roster. Former Tiger running back and Ole Miss starter Kewan Lacy, wide receivers coach and former Missouri player L’Damian Washington and even Horatio Fields, who spent four weeks on a contract with Missouri, will all be facing off against their old team. On both sides, specifically the Tigers, Drinkwitz said there is no hard feelings. "The biggest thing is to not make it bigger than it is," Drinkwitz said. "You have great memories there, there was great things that happened there. From all intents and purposes, I think everybody left in a positive light with both sides... home.blurb: Simmons, top receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. weren’t made available to speak Tuesday about transferring from Ole Miss, but it’s worth noting that Simmons’ Instagram account still has a number of posts from his years in Oxford. “I feel like those guys are definitely going to come out and play with a chip on their shoulder,” tailback Jamal Roberts said. “We definitely can let them guys handle that.” No. 9 Ole Miss reached the College Football Playoff semifinals a season ago with Trinidad Chambliss at quarterback after Simmons went down early with an injury and lost his starting job. Tigers coach Eli Drinkwitz acknowledged that the game will be a big deal for Simmons, along with two other Mizzou players imported from Ole Miss. Drinkwitz just wants them to keep perspective, considering about 20% of FBS players are transfers. “The biggest thing is to not make it bigger than it is,” Drinkwitz told reporters Tuesday. “There are great memories from there. I think everybody left there in a positive light on both sides.” “We talk about the joy of the journey,” Drinkwitz said. “That was a part of their journey that made them who they are right now. I don’t think there has to be a whole lot more to it than that.” Mizzou (5-1, 2-1 Southeastern Conference) comes in having won two straight home games against SEC foes, most recently 27-6 over Texas A&M on Saturday. The Tigers’ biggest win so far came against Florida, 45-17 on Oct. 3. Simmons has been terrific for the Tigers, ranking 11th in FBS in passing efficiency rating. He’s completing 65% of his passes, with 14 touchdowns and one interception in 165 attempts. “He’s playing as an experienced quarterback in a really good system,” Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said. Lee has scored five touchdowns while leading the Tigers with 42 receptions and 616 yards. He and Simmons may be transfers, but they’re already leaders at Mizzou, other players say. Roberts will be another focal point for Ole Miss. After putting together two straight games of 200-plus yards, he ranks first in the SEC and second nationally with 828 rushing yards. Mizzou’s top back a season ago, Ahmad Hardy, is recovering from an offseason gunshot wound. Golding said that Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1 SEC) will have its hands full trying to tackle Roberts. “He has the most yards after contact right now, which is something that has been an issue for us on tape,” Golding said. With Chambliss continuing to rank as a Heisman Trophy contender and NFL prospect, Ole Miss routed Vanderbilt 52-17 on Saturday. The Rebels also have wins against ranked opponents LSU and Louisville. “They’re a total team,” Drinkwitz said. “We need to play our best, most complete game to even be in the game.” In Mizzou’s most recent road game, the Tigers blew a fourth-quarter lead and lost at Mississippi State. As usual, the game has ACC and national title race implications , though this season those conversations are focused far more on Miami, which finished last season as the national runner-up and is currently the heavy favorite to win the ACC in 2026. Things are far different for Florida State and embattled coach Mike Norvell, who entered the year facing serious job pressure and now risks falling to 3-4 on the season and 1-3 in ACC play if the Seminoles cannot pull a stunning upset. Wins against Miami in 2021, 2022 and 2023 were crucial building blocks of Norvell's eventual ACC Championship run, but now it's Mario Cristobal who has the chance to string together three straight wins in the series after the Hurricanes got the better of Florida State in 2024 and 2025. The return to Miami Gardens also spotlights what has become a notable home-field advantage for Miami in this recent run, as the Hurricanes are 15-1 at home since the start of the 2024 season, including that 36-14 win against the Seminoles in Hard Rock Stadium two years ago. Miami has been absolute rock stars in the ACC and the sport as a whole, continuing the momentum from the team's College Football Playoff run with eye-popping scores and stat-stuffing performances to start the 2026 season. Florida State hopes to provide more resistance than the average Miami opponent, but even that might not be enough to stop the ACC's most potent national title contender. Miami vs. Florida State: Need to know A big stage for Darian Mensah's Heisman Trophy case: Miami quarterback Darian Mensah has been playing at an elite level all season, but the lopsided wins and predicted blowouts haven't given him the stage and audience that Saturday night's rivalry game will command. Miami may be in a far better place than Florida State this season, but this iconic rivalry will still bring the attention of Heisman Trophy voters to Hard Rock Stadium to see how Mensah performs under the pressure. Currently, he's one of just two FBS quarterbacks with 15-plus passing touchdowns and zero interceptions and boasts the best completion percentage (84.2%) and passer rating (212.2) in all of FBS. Mensah will still have a road trip to Notre Dame and a few other opportunities to shine in the spotlight, but Saturday night could prove to be the launching point for Mensah to push Jeremiah Smith in the Heisman conversation. Florida State struggling against top teams : While Florida State has won three national championships and spent 72 weeks ranked No. 1 in the AP Top 25 poll throughout its history, the Seminoles have struggled against the best teams in recent years. As the Seminoles take aim at their rival from the South, they do so staring down a brutal losing streak against top-3 teams from the AP poll. Florida State has lost its last eight games against AP top-three teams, last winning in the BCS National Championship Game against Auburn at the end of the 2013 season. Another losing streak that Florida State can put to bed on Saturday night is a 12-game road losing streak against teams with any AP ranking, which stretches back to a 2016 win at Miami. No one is beating teams like Miami is in 2026 : The Hurricanes enter this annual rivalry checkpoint with one of the most dominant teams in the country, beating opponents by an average of 39.8 points per game. That's the largest points-per-game differential through five games in school history and is currently the largest among all FBS teams. Now, a skeptic would be quick to point out that a 70-point win against Florida A&M will do a lot to juice those averages, but it's the consistency with which Miami has been blitzing its opponents that stands out. Of Miami's five games, only one (a 33-20 win at Wake Forest ) was decided by less than 28 points. Where to watch Miami vs. Florida State live Date : Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time : 7 p.m. ET Location : Hard Rock Stadium -- Miami Gardens, Fla. TV: ESPN | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Miami vs. Florida State prediction, picks Miami isn't just blowing teams out on the scoreboard this season; it's a team that's also been exceeding oddsmakers' expectations nearly every week. The Hurricanes indeed have the best point differential in FBS (+39.8), but they also rank T-14 nationally with a 4-1 record against the spread and carry the 15th-best cover margin in the country, beating the spread by an average of 7.8 points per game. With those kinds of trends, it's tough to think that Miami is a candidate for an upset alert, and Florida State's road woes make it very possible that this game will get sideways on the Seminoles. The Seminoles have no answer for a nearly unstoppable Hurricanes offense, and I'm taking the hosts to obliterate their team total in my Florida State vs. Miami prediction. Keep reading for my free college football picks for what should be a high-scoring affair on Saturday, Oct. 17. Who will win Florida State vs Miami: Florida State +21.5 (52%) The Miami Hurricanes are a national championship contender and in a completely different class than the Florida State Seminoles this season, but this large a spread gives me pause. The Seminoles have shown a willingness to push the pace and go into shootouts even in a losing effort, and that has already led to relatively close losses to the likes of the Alabama Crimson Tide and SMU Mustangs . I see that approach as having some bite against a Miami defense that ranks just 27th in the nation in adjusted EPA allowed per play -- a surprisingly mundane number for a team with outstanding raw defensive numbers. I'm taking Florida State to cover as long as the number is 21.5 points or more. Florida State vs Miami Over/Under pick: Over 55.5 (52%) Few games have more signs pointing to a shootout than this one. Miami has one of the country's most efficient offenses, averaging 8.2 yards per play and completing an incredible 83% of its passes. That lines up against a Seminoles defense ranked outside the top 100 in nearly every major metric, including yards allowed per play (6.1) and opposing quarterback rating (140.9). away.headline: Initial week 7 injury report for Florida State vs. No. 3 Miami could spell disaster for the Seminoles
away.blurb: Florida State needs some luck on its side to take down Miami, but that might not happen with multiple players notably absent from the initial injury report . The Hurricanes had two starters in particular suffer injuries last time out against Clemson, but neither player was included in the injury report, which means the Seminoles will be getting the best version of Miami in Week 7. DB Romanas Frederique Jr. (out) LB Noah LaVallee (questionable) No Lightfoot and no McCoy on the injury report likely means Florida State will be playing against a full-strength Miami team. The Hurricanes have a few players who have been ruled out for the game, but nothing serious has changed from last week. That could be an issue for the Seminoles, who already will face two serious mismatches in Week 7. The Hurricanes' offense could also receive a boost if McCoy avoids having to sit out the Week 7 game against the Seminoles. There is no two ways about it, Florida State has struggled to generate consistent pressure on opposing quarterbacks this season. The performance against Virginia in Week 5 was exceptional, but it should be viewed as the outlier at this point, with more disappointing performances than positive ones on defense. Florida State is just days away from perhaps the biggest game on the schedule against ACC rivals No. 3 Miami. The Hurricanes have displayed arguably the best offense and the best defense in the country this season, while the Seminoles have struggled to play consistent football. Starting edge rusher and Miami's sack leader, Marquise Lightfoot, left the game against Clemson early, but the star defender was not included in the first Week 7 injury report. Additionally, starting right tackle Matthew McCoy was attended to by the training staff against the Tigers, but ultimately played the rest of the game. McCoy was also not included in the initial Week 7 injury report for Miami. Marquise Lightfoot, Matthew McCoy left off Miami's initial injury report for the Florida State game For Miami, getting Lightfoot back would be tremendous due to how quickly he can create an impact on the field. Lightfoot disrupts offenses, and Florida State's best chance at igniting the offense is by giving the football to dynamic running back Ousmane Kromah. The running back has been the one constant this season for the Seminoles' offense, but he may meet his match against Lightfoot. Lightfoot currently has 20 total tackles and five sacks this season, with a sack in each of his last four games. The defender also recorded a sack and two tackles against Clemson before exiting, and while Miami has a lot of talent capable of filling the potential void, nobody creates quite as much chaos as Lightfoot does. It is going to be very hard for Florida State, a team that already struggles with generating pressure, to do so against a team like Miami, who have only allowed five total sacks this season. The Seminoles cannot win this game if quarterback Darian Mensah is given a clean pock

They also have the nation's top adjusted EPA/play and net EPA/play defense. Both of these offenses struggle to convert on third down , and the Sooners have one of the least reliable rushing attacks in the nation. If Baxter misses out for Kentucky, then the Under becomes even more attractive. Meanwhile, the Wildcats have scored just 21 first-quarter points over their last five contests, failing to score in the opening 15 minutes in three of those matches. LSU might have the best mix of talent, and it certainly has the highest-profile head coach, but it has two losses, and one of them was last week in a 35-34 overtime thriller to Kentucky. It's just assumed that Texas will find its way into the College Football Playoff, and maybe get to the SEC Championship first. But it just lost to an Oklahoma team that pulled off an all-time found-a-way 27-24 win in the Red River Rivalry. The Sooners only have one SEC loss – 41-13 to Georgia – but all of a sudden, the second half of the schedule doesn't seem that bad. Kentucky, because it's in the first year of the Will Stein era, and Oklahoma, because it beat Texas – both programs are in a good place. But the winner of this will still be alive in the SEC, and the other almost certainly won't. Kentucky vs Oklahoma: Quick Hits Oklahoma goes on the road for two of the next three weeks, traveling to Mississippi State, hosting South Carolina, and going to Florida. It's a key stretch for Kentucky with Vanderbilt at home next, followed by a date at Tennessee. The two programs have only met three times. Oklahoma won 29-8 in 1982 and 29-7 in 1980, but Bear Bryant's Kentucky won the 1951 Sugar Bowl. Start here – it's just not screwing up. UK turned it over three times in the loss to Alabama, twice in a win over South Alabama, and that's it. No turnovers on the road at Texas A&M and South Carolina, and none last week against LSU. And then there are the penalties – there aren't any. Kentucky is No. 1 in the SEC in fewest penalties and fewest penalty yards, and that matters. The lack of turnovers matters. It all matters, because Oklahoma probably can't pull this off without the Wildcats royally screwing up like Texas did last week. Why Oklahoma Will Win Kentucky needs its running game to rock, and that's going to be a problem. Georgia was able to power away on Oklahoma with a few big runs in the blowout win, but that's been about it. Michigan tried to run a lot, and it did just enough to get by, but it was a struggle. Texas wasn't exactly creative in the way it tried to run, and it got stuffed way too often. The Sooners are 3-0 when they don't allow a touchdown run, and 0-2 when they do. And … Kentucky vs Oklahoma Prediction, Betting Lines Kentucky's only loss came in the one game (Alabama) it failed to hit 100 yards rushing and didn't score a touchdown on the ground. Oklahoma will hold up defensively in a low-scoring game that comes down to a few key late stops, but this won't be easy for a team that failed to hit 300 yards of total offense against anyone but UTEP. Kentucky is 135th in the nation in third down conversions. Oklahoma is third in the nation in third down stops. And that's the ball game. picks.headline: Kentucky vs. Oklahoma prediction: Can Cats build momentum after LSU win?
picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Oklahoma prediction: Can Cats build momentum after LSU win? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Kentucky vs. Oklahoma prediction: Can Cats build momentum after LSU win? Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky had only won three overtime games in program history entering the season. Now the Wildcats have won overtime games in back-to-back weeks. What is the reward for two of the more thrilling victories in UK history? A road matchup with an Oklahoma team coming off an upset of the No. 1 team in the country. First-year coach Will Stein and company could clinch bowl eligibility with a victory in Norman, but the No. 15 Wildcats have much bigger goals after a 5-1 start to the season. Winning at Oklahoma might be enough to catapult Kentucky into the top 12 a projected playoff spot, but a concerning injury list will make that task even harder. Can Kentucky move to 6-1 for the first time since 2021? Here is what you need to know heading into the matchup with Oklahoma. Riding the wave Both teams appear to have a similar challenge this week. Kentucky must avoid a letdown after a week that saw thousands of fans storm Kroger Field to celebrate the 35-34 win over LSU. Oklahoma must avoid a letdown after salvaging something from what had been a disappointing first half of the season with an upset of No. 1 Texas in its biggest rivalry game. "Everybody in this league can beat each other," Stein said. "If you don't play well or to a standard, that's when you get embarrassed. It's our job as a football coach, as a program, to put our guys in a situation to be successful mentally, physically, in every facet of their life. It's always a goal." Oklahoma enters the game ranked 128th nationally in total offense but 15th in total defense. UK ranks 55th in total offense and 101st in total defense. On paper at least, the game provides a compelling matchup of relative strengths versus weaknesses. Oklahoma is a 6.5-point favorite, but Kentucky has already won on the road twice this season. With the teams otherwise evenly matched, which group better handles the emotional roller coaster this week probably has the better chance to win. "You're dealing with 18 to 22-year-olds that read a lot of the noise, whether it's good or bad or in between, and so that's part of our job," Stein said. "It's half football coach, half mental coach." Kentucky wide receiver Kenny Darby (19) runs the ball during last Saturday’s win against LSU. The Wildcats this week travel to Norman, Oklahoma, to face an Oklahoma team that upset then-No. 1 Texas last Saturday. (Ryan C. Hermens/rhermens@herald-leader.com) Playoff watch ESPN reported Thursday the College Football Playoff was nearing a deal to expand to 24 teams next season, but this Kentucky team still has to finish in the top 12 to make the playoff. While the committee will not release its first in-season ranking until Nov. 3, the list of contenders is already becoming clear. Kentucky was slotted 15th in this week's Associated Press poll. That poll has no bearing on the playoff field, but it is the best indication available of the work Stein's team still needs to do. With one spot in the playoff guaranteed to the highest-ranked non-power conference champion, Kentucky likely needs to finish the regular season ranked in the top 11 to be included in the field. To do that, the Wildcats probably need to duplicate the 5-1 record from the first half of the season in the second half. Could Kentucky still reach the playoff at 9-3? It seems likely at least one three-loss SEC team will sneak in after the move to a nine-game conference schedule, but it seems unlikely that team would be Kentucky if Texas A&M and LSU (the two best wins on the resume so far) continue their slides. A win at Oklahoma would boost the resume, even though the Sooners are not currently ranked. It would also give Stein and company some breathing room with road games against ranked foes Tennessee and Missouri still on the schedule. Kentucky football injury report Depth continues to be an issue for Kentucky's defense, with backup linebackers Antwan Smith and Tavion Wallace, backup nickel back Jaden Smith and backup cornerback Grant Grayton all out again this week. Backup defensive lineman Tyler Thomas was also listed as doubtful on Wednesday's SEC availability report. The biggest surprise on the report was star running back CJ Baxter being listed as questionable. Baxter did not mention any injury in his post-LSU interview, so it is unclear if he is dealing with an issue from that game or something that happened in practice this week. Given Baxter's poor injury luck the last two years at Texas, Kentucky fans will be nervously following his status until kickoff. Kentucky running back CJ Baxter is listed as questionable for Saturday’s game at Oklahoma. Tight end Elijah Brown and defensive lineman Kalen Edwards were also listed as questionable. Wide receiver Nic Anderson and cornerback Hasaan Sykes were listed as probable. The situation at linebacker could be helped if Alex Afari is declared eligible by a Jefferson County judge after his latest legal hearing in a lawsuit against the NCAA, but it is unclear when the judge will issue a ruling. UK on Wednesday listed Afari, who has not played since the NCAA won an appeal in the case two weeks ago, as questionable. Kentucky football vs. Oklahoma prediction No team in FBS history has won back-to-back overtime games by one point, so it's fair to wonder if Kentucky has used up its store of magic already. It would be unfair to attribute the past two weeks to luck, though. This Kentucky team has earned its success so far. The challenge is real this week against a defense Stein compared favorably to the Alabama team that shut down Kentucky in the second half of its only loss so far. The good news for Kentucky is Oklahoma's offense has struggled for most of the season. If UK can score in the 20s, its chances increase dramatically. Kentucky 21, Oklahoma 17. The final word "If you don't come to play, you'll get embarrassed in this league. We have to play better than what we played last week. There were a lot of great moments, but there was opportunity as well for growth on our team, in all three phases, and as a coaching staff. That's what we're taking in this week. There's no gimmies. You're playing Oklahoma. Like, if you can't get up for that game, then I don't know if you even have a pulse." — Stein on UK's challenge this week How CJ Baxter is making the most of the second chance offered him at Kentucky Kentucky and Oklahoma both claim a 1950 football championship. picks.headline: Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling
picks.blurb: Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Story by Wildcats Wire Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 14, 2026 at 4:11 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels down to Norman to face the Oklahoma Sooners on Saturday, and both of these teams have plenty of momentum coming into this matchup. Arguably no team in the country has more momentum on their side than the Wildcats right now, coming off back-to-back walk off two-point conversions for the win in overtime. However, Oklahoma came off of their bye week and got a massive win over Texas in the Red River Rivalry game. With that being said, do not let the final score fool you, Oklahoma is still really struggling on offense. Oklahoma's offense will be the worst unit on the field this Saturday, and despite a big 27-24 win over Texas, the issues have not been fixed. The Sooners have scored just six offensive touchdowns since week two. They have only scored over 20 points twice this season, this was week one against UTEP and against Texas where they needed a blocked punt for a touchdown and a pick six to do so. This is a night game in Norman and will present a lot of adversity for Kentucky. The matchup to watch is the Kentucky offense versus the Oklahoma defense, but we will get into that side later. Basically every single offensive metric that you look at to determine offensive success, the Sooners rank bottom five in the SEC. Oklahoma ranks dead last in the conference in all of these statistics: Success rate, Rush SR%, EPA per rush, Explosive play rate and 1D+TD%. They also rank bottom five in the SEC in these statistics: EPA per play, EPA per dropback, Pass SR%, 3rd Down conversion rate, Early Down conversion rate and yards per play. This might be the worst offense Kentucky faces this season unless they can turn things around quickly. Oklahoma ranks first in the SEC in three-and-out rate and negative play percentage. The Sooners have the worst yards per carry average in the FBS. This is a stark contrast because Kentucky's defense ranks top five in the SEC in explosive % allowed and negative % forced. Kentucky's defense has excelled at three things this season: forcing turnovers, forcing negative plays and limiting explosives. This Oklahoma offense has struggled, but they do have some playmakers. The number one guy that should scare you, ironically, is number one Isaiah Sategna. Sategna is a dynamic receiver who is the one guy that can consistently create separation and he is dangerous with the football in his hands. Kentucky has to know where Sategna is on every snap because he is lightning in a bottle when he gets his hands on the football. John Mateer is a reckless but talented quarterback, he made the best throw of his season against Texas to set up the Sooners for the game winning field goal. Mateer threw a perfect back shoulder to Sategna from the far hash. Mateer has arm talent and is a dangerous runner, he immediately looks to run when a pass play breaks down. However, Mateer is extremely turnover prone, even moreso than LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt. Kentucky forced two turnovers on Leavitt, and they need to repeat that on Saturday. They have done a great job of forcing turnovers all season, they did it against Keelon Russell, Marcel Reed, LaNorris Sellers and Leavitt. This defensive line has to get pressure on Mateer to force him to play recklessly. The Wildcats have struggled with scrambling quarterbacks this season, but they were better last week against Leavitt--same thing applies this week with Mateer. Oklahoma as we stated, averages the fewest yards per carry in all of FBS. This is a game where Kentucky should be able to make Oklahoma one dimensional, which is a massive advantage for the Wildcats. The defense has to make Mateer uncomfortable in the pocket and they will have a great chance to win this football game. Kentucky's defense has the opportunity to have their best performance of the season this Saturday. picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Oklahoma game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue October 16, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Kentucky Wildcats Basketball College Basketball Recruiting Kentucky Wildcats Football College Football Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Kentucky Football Odds Kentucky Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Library Community Guidelines Media Resources Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Library Expand Community Guidelines Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Kentucky Wildcats Football Following an emotional win vs. No. 10 LSU, Kentucky heads to Oklahoma to face a Sooners team that just beat No. 1 Texas. What a wild Saturday it was for the Kentucky Football team. The Wildcats escaped with a 35-34 overtime victory over then-No. 10 LSU Tigers inside Kroger Field while rocking the iconic Power K jerseys. The game featured plenty of twists and turns, including trick plays that resulted in LSU touchdowns, explosive plays from Kentucky’s offense and special teams, turnovers, and, most importantly, missed field goals. Through it all, Kentucky remained competitive. With LSU facing a fourth-down situation late in regulation, the Tigers elected to punt rather than go for it. Kentucky then drove down the field in less than two minutes, setting up kicker Adam Zouagui for a field goal to send the game into overtime after he had missed his previous two attempts. Kentucky won the coin toss and elected to play defense first. LSU quickly drove down the field and scored a touchdown. The Wildcats then got their opportunity, and on third-and-10, quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Kenny Darby, who nearly took the ball into the end zone but came up a yard short. CJ Baxter immediately punched it in for a touchdown, leaving Kentucky down by one point. Instead of kicking the extra point to force a second overtime, first-year head coach Will Stein decided to go for the two-point conversion to win the game. The decision paid off. Minchey called his own number on a quarterback draw, found plenty of open space, and crossed the goal line untouched to secure the victory. Kentucky defeated LSU 35-34 in overtime, improving to 5-1 overall and 3-1 in SEC play. The Wildcats are now ranked No. 15 in the AP Top 25 poll. Oklahoma Sooners (3-2, 1-1 in SEC) The Oklahoma Sooners have faced increased scrutiny this season after finishing the 2025 campaign with a 10-3 record and earning a spot in the College Football Playoff. However, their season ended with a 34-24 loss to Alabama in the first round, and Oklahoma has struggled to find consistency this year. The potent offense Oklahoma showcased last season has largely been absent throughout the 2026 campaign. The exceptions came in the season opener against UTEP, when the Sooners cruised to a 51-0 victory, and this past weekend, when they defeated then-No. 1 Texas in the Red River Rivalry. However, not all 27 points against Texas came from the offense. Oklahoma scored a touchdown after blocking and recovering a punt in the end zone, while another touchdown came on a pick-six. The Sooners’ other scoring plays included a rushing touchdown and two field goals. Across their other three games, Oklahoma has averaged just 12.3 points per game, which is disappointing for an offense expected to be productive under quarterback John Mateer. Speaking of Mateer, he has completed 90 of 135 pass attempts for a 66.7% completion rate, totaling 1,038 passing yards, eight touchdowns, and four interceptions this season. Mateer is also a running threat, recording 53 carries for 70 rushing yards. Those numbers fall short of his previous two seasons in terms of passing production. In 2025, Mateer threw for 2,885 yards, while he recorded 3,139 passing yards in 2024. His touchdown-to-interception numbers also tell an interesting story. Mateer threw 14 touchdowns and 11 interceptions in 2025, compared with 29 touchdowns and seven interceptions in 2024. For Oklahoma to defeat Kentucky, the Sooners will need Mateer to take another step forward and help their offense become more consistent. For Kentucky to win in Norman, Kenny Minchey and the offense will have to find a way to pierce the Sooners’ stingy defense and avoid game-breaking turnovers that won Oklahoma the game vs. then-No. 1 Texas. As for other notable Oklahoma players, the receiving corps features wide receiver Isaiah Sategna III, Mateer’s primary target, along with tight end Rocky Beers and wide receiver Trell Harris. Kentucky will need to account for all three playmakers while also limiting the Sooners’ running game, which features Lloyd Avant and Jonathan Hatton Jr. Game: Kentucky Football vs. Oklahoma Sooners Location: Oklahoma Memorial Stadium — Norman, Oklahoma Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: 7:30 p.m. ET TV Info: SEC Network will have the TV broadcast Online Streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening Odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as a 6.5-point underdog . ESPN gives Kentucky a 32.1% chance of winning. Our Early Prediction: Kentucky enters this matchup at 5-1 under first-year head coach Will Stein after a huge upset over LSU, while Oklahoma is coming off a rivalry win over Texas. Both teams could experience an emotional hangover after their big victories, but I believe Kentucky can overcome that challenge and earn another road win. Despite concerns about linebacker injuries, the Wildcats have a chance to improve to 6-1, become bowl-eligible, and remain in the College Football Playoff conversation. home.headline: Kentucky vs. Oklahoma Injury Report: Updates on CJ Baxter, Nic Anderson, and more
home.blurb: For Kentucky, the big news is that running back CJ Baxter is questionable to play this week. Baxter got dinged in the second half of the win over LSU but still finished the game and ran for a touchdown in overtime. He’s been one of the SEC’s best backs thus far, so not having him in Norman would be a major setback for this offense. Wide receiver Nic Anderson, who left last week’s win over LSU with a shoulder injury, is listed as probable, so he should be good to go this week as long as there are no setbacks. Defensive tackle Kalen Edwards, who missed last week, is questionable to play. As expected, linebacker Antwan Smith and cornerback Jaden Smith remain out after suffering injuries at South Carolina. Linebacker Tavion Wallace, out for the past two weeks, is still listed as out. Fellow linebacker Alex Afari Jr. is listed as questionable as he works through the legal process in hopes of regaining eligibility. He’s healthy, so if granted eligibility in the courts, he should play Saturday, but that’s a big if right now. Cornerback Grant Grayton remains out. Reserve defensive end Tyler Thomas is doubtful. Reserve tight end Elijah Brown is questionable. Finally, cornerback Hassan Sykes is probable to play. For Oklahoma, standout left tackle Michael Fasusi is nearing a return from a shoulder injury that has kept him out since Week 1. He’s currently listed as questionable. Starting left guard Eddy Pierre-Louis, who missed last week’s win over No. 1 Texas, is questionable. Backup lineman Fred Hinton is questionable as well. Cornerback Eli Bowen, who missed last week, is questionable to play. Fellow cornerback Jacobe Johnson, who was also out last week, is listed as out for this one. Wide receiver Parker Livingstone, who has six catches for 51 yards this year, is questionable. Running back Tory Blaylock, who has 10 carries for 22 yards, is probable. Tight end Jack Van Dorselaer, who does not have a catch this season, is probable. Finally, linebacker Taylor Heim, running back Xavier Robinson, tight end Trynae Washington, and wide receiver Trell Harris have been ruled out. picks.headline: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction
picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska football is hitting the road for one of its biggest games of the season, and Adam Carriker is breaking it all down on the Carriker Chronicles! Matt Rhule and the Nebraska Cornhuskers are heading to Eugene to face Dan Lanning and the Oregon Ducks in a late-night Big Ten showdown. Both teams are coming off losses, and both have plenty to prove. Can the Huskers bounce back and pull off an upset? Nebraska enters the game at 5-1 after a heartbreaking loss to Curt Cignetti and Indiana. The Huskers showed some good things against the Hoosiers, but once again, they couldn't finish the job. Carriker discusses why Nebraska needs more than another moral victory. At some point, the Huskers have to start winning these big games, especially against talented Big Ten opponents. One of the biggest questions is whether Anthony Colandrea and Nebraska's offense can get things going against Oregon's defense. Colandrea has shown he can make plays, but Carriker believes offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen needs to put him in good situations, especially on third downs. The Huskers also need production from Jamal Rule and the running back rotation. Can Nebraska establish a running game and keep Oregon's defense guessing? On the other side of the ball, Nebraska's Blackshirts face a major challenge. Oregon has talented receivers who can stretch the field and create explosive plays. Carriker looks at Nebraska's defensive numbers and explains why the Huskers cannot allow Oregon to make big plays over the top. The Blackshirts have been improving, but this will be another serious test of just how far they've come. Carriker also breaks down Oregon's defense, including players like Matayo Uiagalelei and Bear Alexander. The Ducks have plenty of talent, but Oregon has also been unpredictable this season. Nebraska cannot afford to let this become the game where everything suddenly clicks for Oregon. This is also Nebraska's stiffest road test so far this year. Playing in Eugene, in front of a loud Oregon crowd, will test the Huskers' experience and mental toughness. Nebraska has added veteran players who have been through big games before. Now it's time to see whether that experience pays off. Carriker shares his four keys to the game: handle Oregon's crowd, execute in the red zone, prevent big plays and play all four quarters. Nebraska must protect Colandrea, finish drives and avoid the mistakes that have cost the Huskers in close games. Finally, Carriker discusses the point spread and makes his score prediction! He's picking Nebraska to pull off the upset, 24-21! Can Matt Rhule and the Huskers shock Oregon, earn their third Big Ten win and make a statement to the rest of college football? Or will Dan Lanning and the Ducks send Nebraska home with another disappointing loss? Get Adam Carriker's full Nebraska-Oregon preview, breakdown and prediction on the Carriker Chronicles! Stay up to date on all things Huskers by bookmarking Nebraska Cornhuskers On SI , following us on Twitter/X , and visiting HuskerMax.com daily. Loading recommendations... He was twice named first-team All-Big 12, leading the conference in sacks and winning the Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year award his senior season, along with several other awards, including finishing with All-America honors, in addition to being named to the Big 12 Commissioner’s Academic Honor Roll three times. He’s also been named to Nebraska’s All-Century Team, voted The Best Husker Defensive End since the start of the new millennium, and has been inducted into the Nebraska Football Hall of Fame. Adam went on to play eight years as a Defensive Lineman in the NFL with the St. Louis Rams and Washington Redskins. He was drafted in the 1st round, winning Rams Rookie of the Year; he’s the only Ram in franchise history to start all 16 games as a rookie. He also won the Strongest Redskin award multiple times during his career in the NFL. Since retiring, he’s experienced great success in the business world and has also appeared multiple times on National Television and Radio Shows, and currently hosts his highly popular show, the Carriker Chronicles, aka, the People’s Show, which has been viewed by millions! Thomas replaced the wildly inefficient Raiola in the fourth quarter and accounted for 156 of the team’s 272 total yards on the day. If Raiola gets the starting nod under center, he’ll be facing his former team in Nebraska, where he passed for 4,819 yards and 31 touchdowns. Whoever starts for Lanning’s squad will stare across the line at a Huskers’ defense that has simply been dominant. Nebraska is allowing just 15.2 points and 276.2 yards per game with the nation’s best third-down defense (19.7 percent), ahead of No. 2 Oregon (22.1 percent). After the 17-15 loss to the now No. 12 UCLA Bruins (5-0, 3-0 Big Ten) inside Autzen Stadium and Moore looking to move off of concussion protocol, no more mistakes can be made if a third straight College Football Playoff appearance is to be made. The over/under is set at 52.5. The last time these two opponents met was in the 2017 campaign, resulting in a 42-35 victory for the Ducks in Eugene, Oregon. That's as long as Moore is fully cleared to suit back up after suffering a concussion in the 41-27 victory at the USC Trojans back on Sept. 26. If Moore doesn't, will Sheldon product Thomas receive his first career start with Oregon? Will an offensive play-caller change be made after first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer conjured up only 272 total yards from the press box? Under Mehringer, the Ducks committed a total of seven turnovers to the Bruins, tied for the most since their 30-24 loss to Indiana in the Pacific Northwest back on Sept. 11, 2004. Raiola struggled to take care of the ball against coach Bob Chesney's defense, completing only 6-of-19 passes for 43 passing yards, zero touchdowns, and two interceptions. Not to mention his one lost fumble. Oregon as a whole only went 1-for-12 on third downs and 0-for-2 on fourth downs. That mental mistake by the referees was an oversight that might have cost the Ducks their chance at any sort of deep postseason run.
