picks.blurb: 'I Will Ride or Die with Anthony Colandrea': Matt Rhule Recaps Nebraska's Loss to Indiana, Previews Oregon Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska head coach Matt Rhule knows 55 minutes of good football isn't enough. It might be against some teams, but not most. As the Huskers look to bounce back from a three-point loss to defending national champion Indiana , Rhule and his staff are making that a point of emphasis for the entire team. At the same time, Rhule is willing to bet on his quarterback to get the job done. Meeting with the media Monday, Rhule reiterated that message and shed light on the Big Red's preparations for its Week 7 road game against the Oregon Ducks. Here's everything he had to say. Anthony Colandrea looks to pass against Indiana. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NU led for much of the game Saturday afternoon, yet the Hoosiers came crawling back. Even when Indiana took the lead late in the fourth quarter, Rhule was still willing to bet on Colandrea to make a play. NU led for much of the game Saturday afternoon, yet the Hoosiers came crawling back. Even when Indiana took the lead late in the fourth quarter, Rhule was still willing to bet on Colandrea to make a play. Asked about going for it on fourth-and-nine, the head coach pointed to what the analytics said: Go for it. It didn't work out this time, but he said he'd do it again. “I just felt like I was going to follow the analytics and put the ball in Anthony’s hands,” Rhule said. “We had holes that we thought were open and felt like, if we wanted to win that game, that ball and that field position, when you needed about 20 yards to kick a field goal, I’m going to put it in Colandrea's hands.” “I don’t always follow the analytics,” he continued. “I felt like our defense would get the stop, but more importantly, I just felt like I needed to put this ball in my guys' hands. I will ride or die with Anthony Colandrea all day, every day.” Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti and FOX Sports' Joel Klatt walk on the sideline during warmups before Saturday's game. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There's no shame in losing to perhaps the best coach in college football in 2026. Still, Nebraska had the Hoosiers on the ropes and failed to put them away. There's no shame in losing to perhaps the best coach in college football in 2026. Still, Nebraska had the Hoosiers on the ropes and failed to put them away. Rhule knows the Huskers need to be better in a few key moments, like that fourth-and-nine, but he doesn't believe the team needs to overhaul much. “When we watched the tape on Sunday, I think you have a team that is angry, who knows they let one get away,” he said. “We’re certainly disappointed, but not discouraged. We also understand that that is what it looks like. You have to not play really well for 55 minutes, you have to play well for 60.” “I think each and every one of us: coaches, staff, players, knows that we have to be one or two plays better,” he continued. “I’ve encouraged the guys to take this time to be one or two plays better, every one of us, so that we can win that game when it comes back in the future.” Kyle Cunanan kicks a PAT last season. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The offense wasn't the only unit that missed an opportunity to make a play. Nebraska's special teams failed to convert a 40-yard field goal late in the first half, a miss that proved costly in the three-point loss. The offense wasn't the only unit that missed an opportunity to make a play. Nebraska's special teams failed to convert a 40-yard field goal late in the first half, a miss that proved costly in the three-point loss. Even so, Rhule still has confidence in his specialists. NU is just 3-for-7 on field-goal attempts in 2026, but the Huskers' head coach said a strong week of practice would influence his decision to trust the kicking game moving forward. “I don’t know if it was perfect, but that’s one we should make,” said Rhule. “I think we’ve had our share of issues so far… We had a missed extra point against Maryland. We had a bad snap against Maryland… I can’t live in a world of confident (or) not confident. I have to err on the side of going for it.” “If we have a great week of practice, then I’ll lean towards that (kicking),” he continued. “But with Anthony, we basically have been like, ‘Hey, we’re going to try to play four downs’. Not because we don’t trust our field goal game, but because we believe in the weapons we have on offense… But yeah, it’s just something we’ve got to get cleaned up this week before we go to Oregon.” Football out west. 🗓️ 10.17.26 ⏰ 10:00 PM CT 🏟️ Autzen Stadium vs Oregon 📺 @CFBONFOX pic.twitter.com/Cy6UNrS913 Nebraska's game at Oregon will feature the latest kickoff time Rhule has ever coached, with the game certain to extend into the early hours of Sunday morning Central time. To prepare for that, NU is pushing its practices back a two hours and asking players to adjust their sleep schedules. “I had read some of the things that P.J. Fleck had done, I had read some of the things that Charles Huff at Memphis had done, and a lot of it just goes into sleep,” he said. “We’re really asking our guys to go to bed a little bit later each night this week.” “We’re going to finish this game at 2 a.m. our time,” he continued. “Your circadian rhythm starts to shut down, so we’re really just trying, as best as we can, to make 2 a.m. become 12 a.m., make 12 a.m. become 10 p.m. in terms of our bodies this week.” Anthony Colandrea carries the ball against Indiana. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Having a veteran team likely helps, but so does having a quarterback who sets the tone for the entire team. Colandrea, who carried the ball 17 times for 47 yards and a touchdown Saturday, is one player Rhule probably won't have to worry about getting ready to play. Having a veteran team likely helps, but so does having a quarterback who sets the tone for the entire team. Colandrea, who carried the ball 17 times for 47 yards and a touchdown Saturday, is one player Rhule probably won't have to worry about getting ready to play. Despite Colandrea's heavy workload in Week 6, Rhule maintained his stance on trusting the quarterback to remain productive while making smart decisions to protect his health. "I want him to play," said Rhule. "Dante (Moore, Oregon's quarterback) got hurt sliding, you know? Other guys are getting hurt sliding as well. Would I like Anthony to run the ball out of bounds? Certainly, but he's also cutting back on the zone read and making that game 17-6." "If you have a Porsche, you better let it drive 180," he continued. "I know everything I say gets blown into a little tidbit; I'm not saying he's a Porsche; I'm just saying I think it would be unwise to have a player like Anthony and not let him play to his full ability." This is the season for an Oregon team that should be in full rock-and-roll mode at this point, but instead it's been one big, sad trombone of a season. The Ducks are still 3-2 with a not-that-horrible schedule the rest of the way outside of a trip to Ohio State. They lost to UCLA, but they can stay alive in the Big Ten title hunt with one more loss, even if an at-large CFP bid is likely gone with a third defeat and no Big Ten Championship. And they have to do it with Nebraska's former star quarterback, Dylan Raiola – maybe. Nebraska had Indiana cooked, but it turned the stove off too early. The Hoosiers rallied back for a 20-17 win, but that might have been more about the defending national champs not being as good this year than the Huskers being close to fantastic. However, winning in Eugene is still hard, and if Nebraska can do it, it's 6-1 with a favorable schedule – Ohio State comes to Lincoln – and all of a sudden, it's on the fast track to 10-2 – at least – and a possible at-large CFP bid. Nebraska vs Oregon: Quick Hits Oregon ends a good run of home games and goes to Illinois after this. After that, it hosts Northwestern before going to Ohio State. Nebraska starts a run of three road games in four dates, getting a week off before playing Washington, and then it's off to Illinois. The two have never played as Big Ten teams. Oregon won the last meeting 42-35 in 2017. The Huskers are 6-2 overall in the series, with the first win in 1952. How To Watch Nebraska vs Oregon Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Game Time: 11:00 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Autzen Stadium, Eugene, OR – CFN Week 7 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Week 7 Expert Picks Why Nebraska Will Win UCLA beat up, battered, and bruised Oregon last week. The Ducks might have knocked out Bruin quarterback Nico Iamaleava with a knee injury, but they were destroyed offensively with seven turnovers and just 272 yards of total offense. Oregon is a mess. Star quarterback Dante Moore is expected to miss another game after suffering a concussion against USC. Dylan Raiola might get his shot against his former team, but he was beyond awful against UCLA. Brock Thomas doesn't have Raiola's talent, but he got the offense moving in the second half. Nebraska gave up two huge touchdowns against Indiana, but held firm the rest of the way. Oregon's offensive problems won't all of a sudden be fixed this week. Oct 10, 2026; Lincoln, Nebraska, USA; Nebraska Cornhuskers quarterback Anthony Colandrea (10) passes against the Indiana Hoosiers during the second quarter at Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dylan Widger-Imagn Images Why Oregon Will Win Lost in all of Oregon's misery is a defense that showed up and tried to save the day against UCLA. It's been the only team able to stuff the Bruin running game, and it should do the same against Nebraska, starting by keeping quarterback Anthony Colandrea from doing much on the move. The Huskers can force takeaways – three against Michigan State, two against Maryland – but the Ducks are capable of getting their running game moving a bit to take the pressure off the passing game. And about the quarterback situation, yes, Bob Chesney and the UCLA defense pitched a gem last week. But the week before that, Raiola stepped in and threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns in a brilliant fill-in performance for Moore against USC. Nebraska vs Oregon Prediction, Betting Lines This is too fluid to be definitive – Oregon might rotate quarterbacks no matter who starts – but this will be more on the Duck defense. It'll be fantastic against the Nebraska running game, and that will be enough. Oregon is 3-0 when allowing fewer than 140 yards on the ground, and Nebraska managed just 128 against Indiana. This won't be pretty, but it'll be a fascinating late-night battle with a few more points than you might expect. The Nebraska Cornhuskers took the defending champion Indiana Hoosiers to the wire, leading for over three quarters before eventually falling 20-17 to the top five team. But sadly, it wasn't meant to be for Anthony Colandrea (pictured above, pointing to Will Compton en route to a 39-yard touchdown that put the Huskers up 17-6, seemingly icing the game for Big Red) and Company, as Herbert Hoover found Nick Marsh for two fourth-quarter scores, keeping the visitors from Bloomington unbeaten. It was, of course, Nebraska's first loss of the season. This team will go the way of its quarterback. How far can Anthony Colandrea carry the Nebraska Cornhuskers? That depends on if every defense will drop eight into coverage and rush three. Three of those eight in coverage are likely SPIES working for the enemy. Well, spies spying on our beloved quarterback. AC also had a few bad throws, struggling to feed his receivers catchable passes. For the first time this season, Nebraska did not throw a touchdown pass. The running game barely scraped by the century mark. Big plays crushed the defense. But if you looked at this game and don't see progress, you're being willfully ignorant. The Huskers controlled the ball, nearly doubling the time of possession. Nebraska was the more physical team, and the defense shut down two prominent opposing rushers. Now Big Red travels to Eugene to face the Oregon Ducks. Oregon just lost to UCLA, benched Dylan Raiola for a former walk-on, and was bumped from the Top 25. Needless to say, it's been a big week for the Ducks. Let's look at what the experts are saying. Vegas oddsmakers believe that this is a much better Nebraska team than what they predicted in the summer. Before the season, the spread for this game was 21.5 points. Immediately after the Nebraska/Indiana game, the spread was 12.5 points. Then Oregon lost to the Bruins. As of this writing, the FanDuel Sportsbook has the home Ducks as a 7.5-point favorite. While it will be a reunion for Oregon football quarterback Dylan Raiola taking on his former school in Nebraska, this college football insider makes a point that it probably won't be him starting on Saturday. According to Justin Hopkins at On3 Sports, the quarterback that "has the leg up" is Brock Thomas, though this is all dependent on whether Dante Moore can come back from a concussion. "Based on what I've heard, Brock Thomas has the leg up," Hopkins wrote. "My bet, today, is that he will be the guy running out with the offense first Saturday night. That's because of what he brings to the table for the offense, the consistency, and because of what he was able to do late in the game Saturday night vs. UCLA." Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Oregon football's Dylan Raiola was rough in loss to USC As Moore was taken out of the Sept. 26 41-27 win over the USC Trojans with a concussion, Raiola took over and finished off the win, but it was a frustrating effort in the aforementioned loss to UCLA. In that contest, Raiola threw for 43 yards and two picks before being taken out for Thomas, who recorded 156 yards and a touchdown while completing 11 of his 15 pass attempts. While there would be a lot of attention around Raiola starting and playing against his former team in the Cornhuskers, there's a good chance that won't be the reality, especially if Moore came back to play. "This game — of course, it's going to be an emotional game for Dylan, being the place he came from. He's going to do everything he can to make sure our team is in the best situation to have success this week and be prepared. … I know he'll do that because he's a pro," Lanning said Monday, per Pete Nakos. It remains to be seen what the quarterback situation looks like Saturday for the Oregon football program against Nebraska. away.headline: Oregon Star Evan Stewart's Injury Status Changes vs. Nebraska
away.blurb: With coach Dan Lanning and his team searching for answers offensively, injury woes certainly haven’t helped the Ducks’ hopes of keeping their season alive. Dante Moore’s ‘Out’ designation on the injury report for the second week in a row raises questions about the starting quarterback position. The only addition to the second injury report was offensive lineman Dave Iuli listedas probable after not being on the first report. Stewart's availability, however, moved from questionable to doubtful. Below are the players listed as out, doubtful, questionable and probable. This is the second of four required injury reports from the Big Ten, which start three days ahead of the game. Oregon’s next injury report is expected at 5 p.m. PT on Friday. McClellan continues to be listed as unavailable, while a Stewart absence could mean two of the Ducks’ top three receivers are out against the Cornhuskers. Stewart leads the Ducks in receptions (27), receiving yards (352) and is tied for the lead in receiving touchdowns (four) through five games. He’s scored in each of the last four outings. If Stewart is out, that puts more pressure on sophomore Dakorien Moore. Moore also has four receiving touchdowns this season, along with 18 receptions for 311 yards. Dan Lanning’s Akili Smith Jr. Comments Take on New Meaning With Dante Moore Out The Oregon Ducks’ second loss of the season puts the program in must-win mode entering a pivotal matchup with the Nebraska Cornhuskers. Meanwhile, Oregon is without a starting safety in Aaron Flowers and continues to be without key receiver Jeremiah McClellan. The first injury report revealed that the Ducks’ receiver depth may have taken an additional hit, with all eyes waiting for Evan Stewart’s updated status on Thursday. Oregon Ducks Injury Report vs. Nebraska Cornhuskers Wide receiver Jeremiah McClellan Offensive lineman Trent Ferguson Oregon’s Receiver Depth is Tested McClellan was the first big loss at receiver for Oregon after being a late scratch right before the Portland State Vikings game. Lanning said that McClellan broke his foot in warmups. The receiver was an option to be at the top of the depth chart in 2026 in his third season. home.headline: Another Husker safety ruled out, standout Oregon receiver now doubtful
home.blurb: Here's the latest injury report. Another Husker is out for Saturday's game and one of Oregon's top receivers is doubtful. Nebraska is now down two safeties from its two-deep for Saturday's game. One of Oregon's key receivers who could try to burn them might not be out there, either. It was already known that the Huskers would be without starting safety Jamir Conn. Thursday's report showed that safety Rex Guthrie is also out. He hadn't been on Wednesday's report. Guthrie has battled injuries this season, with his snaps limited to 42, all in nonconference play. But he seemed like a potentially important option, especially with Conn out, given the 574 snaps he logged last year. Evan Stewart, the Ducks' standout wide receiver, is now doubtful for Saturday night's game against Nebraska in Eugene. He was questionable the night before. Stewart has 352 yards and four touchdowns on 27 catches. The Husker injury report also included the addition of backup offensive lineman Preston Taumua, who is listed as probable. Wednesday's report had already laid out Nebraska's biggest injury concerns, with Conn declared out and defensive tackle Riley Van Poppel listed as doubtful. After missing Saturday's 20-17 loss to Indiana, Van Poppel remained doubtful Thursday. "Jamir's a unique spirit. We'll miss having him out there with us both in terms of his play, and also his leadership," Rhule said. "But we have other guys. Caleb Benning is ready to step in. We have other guys that are tremendous leaders. Whether it's Owen Chambliss, Owen Stoudmire, Ant Jones, or many, many more, they'll certainly fill that void." On Tuesday, before the first injury report, Husker defensive coordinator Rob Aurich spoke about the outlook if Conn were unavailable. "It's going to be a great, great test for everybody else in that room and who steps up and how we find the best combination of the best 11 players on the field," Aurich said, adding, "Let's say, for whatever reason, someone isn't available, it's not always that we have to replace them with a safety or a corner. Ducks coach Dan Lanning has also mentioned Akili Smith Jr. as a possibility.
